`Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.pinField`. Turns the stored polynomial constraint coefficients into the period-one matrix field Ξᵢ. The action on a perturbation is defined elsewhere.

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.labelDensity`. Evaluates the full mode form using the parameter's period, weights and bounds at time zero and angle zero. It is the reduced Iι density, before multiplication by r.

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.stretchPosMean`. Averages the positive part of the stretching expression over time and angle. Taking the positive part before averaging differs from taking the positive part of the averaged expression.

`Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.formPos`. Adds the sum of positive mode-density integrals and the mean positive stretching integral, with cylindrical weight r. Its value lies in the extended nonnegative reals and can be infinite.

`Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsModeClass`. Requires positive azimuthal order and membership of the half-time rotation and spatial flip in Γ. This predicate alone does not say that every element of Γ is generated by them.
[`order_pos`](https://github.com/tristanbuckmaster/navier-stokes/blob/ad53419de079eb8f95f60313473374624a348546/lean/CellLayerChallenge.lean#L1972)

Γ contains the spatial flip with zero time shift.

Right-hand-side field in the linearized equation.

F is jointly almost-everywhere strongly measurable in time and space.

The squared norm of F is integrable over one normalized time period and all of space.
F satisfies the linearized equation with β against divergence-free compact test fields, hence modulo gradients.

`Breakdown.CertCell.ContinuumConditionsGiven`. Collects enclosure admissibility, reflection symmetry and a global coefficient-floor witness. The same three enclosure constants must work for every α.
One triple of enclosure constants establishes admissibility for every allowed parameter.
The piece and bound values satisfy the harmonic reflection clauses at every parameter.
There exists one global coefficient-bound entry satisfying all coverage and floor conditions.
`Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.lowStrain`. Selects one component and two polynomial degrees of a resolved harmonic's gradient; the cutoff is Q+1 in each direction.
`Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.lowVelocity`. Selects one velocity component with both polynomial degrees below Q. Its degree range is one shorter than the gradient block.
`Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.sideVelocity`. Selects a side, component and test degree below q+2 for a resolved harmonic.
`Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.sideGradient`. Selects the side derivative moment with degrees below q+1, a different range from side velocity moments.
`Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.cornerVelocity`. Selects a labelled velocity component at a corner. Axis corners can instead be absent from the layout through an optional lookup.
`Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.cornerStream`. Selects a corner stream value without a harmonic label. This block contributes one coordinate per corner, not one per harmonic.

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.extraVelocity`. Selects one of four whole-cell sides and a polynomial test degree through Q. These coordinates are later related to the segmented side moments.

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.SkeletonKey`. A key records the harmonic, geometric face or corner, component and test polynomial data. Interior coordinates receive a private tag and are not identified as boundary values by this key alone.

`Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.keyOf`. Converts each skeleton block into its geometric key, retaining the full test-coefficient function. Volume and extra-side coordinates are sent to the private constructor.

`Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsOffModeCondition`. The region is a measurable subset of the open quarter-plane, and the charged scalar form must pass (B.29) at every point there.

`Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeRadius`. The radius √(r²+z²) is the full spatial distance |y| in cylindrical coordinates, not the cylindrical radius r.
`Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeRayRegion`. The exterior is the part of the open quarter-plane lying strictly beyond the direction-dependent radius.
`Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeSquareExterior`. A point belongs when either r or z exceeds the supplied edge, still restricted to r>0 and z>0.
`Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsDirectionRadius`. The radius function is measurable, uniformly bounded above and below by a positive number, and homogeneous of degree zero under positive dilations.

The region and Λ₀ fit either the radial-graph branch or the zero-azimuthal square-exterior branch.

Full radius times the cross coefficient is at most f₀₁∞.

The cross ceiling f₀₁∞ is nonnegative.
The combined velocity and cross costs fit beneath f₁∞ as in (B.30).

`Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientConditions`. The complement condition quantifies every label and every point with r>0 and z≥0, including points outside all cells. The velocity coefficient floor is weighted by r²+z².

Periods, weights and harmonic support sets have their required positivity and symmetry properties.
The local forms, global rows, tree, gauges and exterior covers satisfy their shared entry conditions.
The particular enclosure numbers in N work for every allowed parameter.
The certificate’s L² coercive constant dominates the explicit enclosure-derived bound.
The certificate’s pin constant is at least √(pinWeight/coercivity).
The direct Section 7 sign and numerical inequalities hold.
The profile, pressure and adjoint shape entries decode to the certificate’s actual fields and satisfy their bounds.
The offset expansion and its interior/exterior bounds are valid for the shared fields.
The centre and parameter-set errors meet the gap and frozen-form shift budgets.
The reference model supplies the required frozen-form lower bound.
The chosen numbers bound the adjoint quadratic terms.
Adjoint fields, offsets and defect entries agree, including the empty fitted-set specialization.
The adjoint potentials and pin fields come from valid, exactly linked shape data.
Every selected adjoint coordinate satisfies its full dual-defect bound.

Breakdown.SteadyCert.FracCertData.text: This record supplies the abstract profile, multiplier, row and adjoint data used by reusable cell estimates. Its spatial profiles and rotation rate belong to the steady interface; the active Appendix B certificate later uses time-periodic CellLayerData.

Breakdown.CellCert.permSign.text: The alternating sign fixes the curl convention in cylindrical component arrays. Repeated indices contribute zero; the order of the two gradient indices matters.

Breakdown.CellCert.FracCellData.text: This extends the steady-certificate record with a region, polynomial-model fields, approximation losses and spectral bounds. The fields are inputs; validity and error inequalities are supplied by separate predicates.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.pinFiel.text: Turns the stored polynomial constraint coefficients into the period-one matrix field Ξᵢ. The action on a perturbation is defined elsewhere.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.labelDe.text: Evaluates the full mode form using the parameter's period, weights and bounds at time zero and angle zero. It is the reduced Iι density, before multiplication by r.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.stretch.text: Averages the positive part of the stretching expression over time and angle. Taking the positive part before averaging differs from taking the positive part of the averaged expression.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.formPos.text: Adds the sum of positive mode-density integrals and the mean positive stretching integral, with cylindrical weight r. Its value lies in the extended nonnegative reals and can be infinite.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsModeClass.text: Requires positive azimuthal order and membership of the half-time rotation and spatial flip in Γ. This predicate alone does not say that every element of Γ is generated by them.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.HasMeasurableB.text: Requires measurable transport bounds, four harmonic amplitudes and the two global suprema. These hypotheses make the ensuing integrals meaningful; a finite table needs an accompanying construction argument.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsHarmonicExpa.text: Requires exact finite reconstruction of the field, its gradient and its supplied Hessian, with a label set closed under negation. It is an identity for every point, not a numerical truncation estimate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.azimuthPhase.text: Uses only the spatial integer nκ and angle. The time phase has already been separated when this helper is used.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.patch.text: Builds the closed rectangle [ρ₁,ρ₂]×[0,h] used for trace-credit estimates. The definition does not require positive width or height.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.patchGradSq.text: Adds the two meridian derivative squares and the angular term k²|φ|²/r². Its geometric use needs the positive-radius patch conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.PlaneSegment.text: Stores a radial interval, patch height and a finite family of real test functions. Their regularity is required by a separate predicate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsPlaneSegment.text: Requires a positive inner radius, positive width and height and continuity of every test. These conditions avoid the axis singularity in the Dirichlet density.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.CrossWaveEntry.text: Stores angular modes of the strain and supplied second-derivative data, their bounds, and positive splitting parameters. The actual operator inequalities are in IsCrossWaveEntry.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsCrossWaveEnt.text: Bounds the symmetric strain and reconstructed vorticity-gradient operators for every point, angle and complex vector. Sampling a matrix at finitely many angles is not this predicate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsInstanceEn.text: Rows, weights, forcing fields, pin fields and the symmetry set are linked to one CellLayerData object here.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyHess.text: This is the iterated Fréchet derivative of the complex vector term. Its pointwise values at spline knots are later replaced on the reference-profile route.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.realPartVe.text: The coordinatewise real part is packaged as a real continuous linear map so that it can be composed with derivative maps.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeHess.text: Second-derivative maps of the individual harmonic terms are summed and passed through the real-part map.

Breakdown.CertReduction.gapGradCoeff.text: The Boolean selects either the L³ Sobolev coefficient 2/(√3√w_*) or the L² route through the supremum bound c_w.

Breakdown.CertReduction.shiftGradCoeff.text: The cubic branch uses half the gap coefficient because the form estimate combines ∇u and ∆u through the weighted energy inequality.

Breakdown.CertReduction.ModelFormNumbers.text: The two stored numbers are s_- and the L³ norm bound on the reference gradient used for c′₃ in (B.48).

Breakdown.CertReduction.FrozenFormBounde.text: The strain lower bound is a quadratic-form bound, while the gradient bound is an L³ integral of the operator norm at each time, uniformly on K.

Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointQuadNumbe.text: For each active adjoint, a Boolean chooses the L³ or L² estimate and a scalar bounds the selected norm.

Breakdown.CertReduction.adjointQuadCoeff.text: The L³ route contributes 2/(√3 w_*), and the L² route contributes c_w/√w_*, before multiplication by n_ψ.

Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointSizeBound.text: The predicate selects the L³ cubed integral or the L² squared integral according to the Boolean; it does not itself require the proposed bound to be nonnegative.

Breakdown.CertReduction.AdjointQuadratic.text: For each j∈J the selected norm is bounded at every time and parameter, its scalar is nonnegative, and the resulting coefficient fits below ãⱼ.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.af.text: The Hessian uses the same centre and tangent decomposition and the same parameter-dependent phase as the field itself.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr.text: The stored second-derivative map is built from the same moving-phase centre and tangent fields as Wᵃ.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is.text: The analytic profile and Hessian equal the decoded constructors for every α, not only α∈K. The target is exactly the pin value of the profile gradient, which removes a separate target gap.
The certificate's pressureGrad is ∇(qα−|Wᵃα|²/2), an exact equality for all α, times and spatial points.
For j∈J the decoded adjoint is independent of α and every harmonic has decay exponent at least 3, as required for the later potential pairings.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.In.text: The predicate collects three exact representation links; it adds no separate numerical inequality.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.withFor.text: Changes only the coefficient c in each parameter-dependent collection of pieces. It leaves the certificate’s own coercivity field unchanged.

Breakdown.CertCell.AdmissibleTuple.text: Packages v, its weak spatial derivatives, the weak similarity transport field g, multipliers β and the right-hand side F. The positive form is finite at the explicitly supplied cForm, which need not be the stored coefficient until a later substitution.

Breakdown.CertCell.ContinuumConditionsGi.text: Collects enclosure admissibility, reflection symmetry and a global coefficient-floor witness. The same three enclosure constants must work for every α.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.text: Selects one component and two polynomial degrees of a resolved harmonic's gradient; the cutoff is Q+1 in each direction.
Selects one velocity component with both polynomial degrees below Q. Its degree range is one shorter than the gradient block.
Selects a side, component and test degree below q+2 for a resolved harmonic.
Selects the side derivative moment with degrees below q+1, a different range from side velocity moments.
Selects a labelled velocity component at a corner. Axis corners can instead be absent from the layout through an optional lookup.
Selects a corner stream value without a harmonic label. This block contributes one coordinate per corner, not one per harmonic.
Selects one of four whole-cell sides and a polynomial test degree through Q. These coordinates are later related to the segmented side moments.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.Skele.text: A key records the harmonic, geometric face or corner, component and test polynomial data. Interior coordinates receive a private tag and are not identified as boundary values by this key alone.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.keyOf.text: Converts each skeleton block into its geometric key, retaining the full test-coefficient function. Volume and extra-side coordinates are sent to the private constructor.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellCoordinates.MeshS.text: Reconstructs the segment's visible geometry and test family, using level+1 as an auxiliary opposite face. This chosen opposite face is not a certificate's physical cell width.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.text: Stores a square complex coefficient array through one degree in each variable. Evaluation uses affine reference coordinates, rather than raw powers of r and z.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.eval.text: Uses powers of the affine reference coordinates refR and refZ. A decoder using raw monomials must convert coefficients exactly.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.zero.text: Represents the zero function with degree zero and a zero coefficient. Higher-degree zero arrays are different data with the same evaluated function.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.text: Stores a finite harmonic set for each cell and a polynomial for every harmonic and component. The harmonic set determines which coefficients participate in the field sum.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.text: Uses two component indices for each cell and label. A coefficient outside the listed harmonics exists in the data function but is absent from the field sum.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModelPolys.text: Collects the four model fields and an approximation to the inverse period. These are approximants with independent error bounds, not exact derivatives by construction.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModelErrors.text: Stores residual and high-part budgets for a decomposition into polynomial, high and long pieces, together with an inverse-period error. The base entries do not alone bound the full field minus its polynomial model.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCharges.text: Stores the three coefficients s₁,s₂,s₃ and the splitting length h of (B.25), as functions of label and meridian point.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.text: Records the cell, label, real or imaginary part and test number of each row, together with test fields and weights. Completeness, independence and normalisation are checked separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerData.text: Combines the extended certificate with its weights, reference field, finite mesh, models, rows, constraints and coercivity constants. The fifteen-field condition later verifies compatibility of these inputs.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCoefficients.text: The five real entries correspond respectively to I₂, I₂′, I₀₁, I₁ and I₀ in (B.16). Their signs are imposed by later inequalities.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellPoly.scale.text: Keeps the stored degree and multiplies every complex coefficient by the same scalar, including the real-versus-imaginary row factor.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.InstanceData.text: The record collects the choices needed to interpret rows, scalar weights and forcing harmonics. It contains functions and permutations, so it is not itself a binary file format.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.KeyAmp.text: The radial and polar entries encode A and B when ι₁≠0; stream, swirl and axisCoef encode S, T and γ when ι₁=0. The unused branch remains present in the record.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ShapeParam.text: The record collects L, κ, f and g, which are shared by the field's harmonic terms.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.TimeFieldD.text: A finite set selects the active (ι,l) keys, while a total amplitude function supplies the data at each key.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenShape.text: The reference profile has its own shape parameters, while every forcing field may use a different length and radial phase with a recorded support edge.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.bit.text: The Boolean indicator is interpreted exactly as 0 or 1 in the coefficient formulas.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr.text: The record stores one common chart/phase, the radial step and rates, and separate centre/tangent harmonic data and origin profiles.
The key set uses the same time/angular/radial phases as the vector-field representation, with scalar amplitudes.
The centre pressure and each tangent pressure have fixed harmonic coefficients; their common radial phase still changes with α.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Ad.text: All active adjoints share one chart/phase record, with a separate finite harmonic field for each index.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellVar.text: The dependent sum retains each resolved lattice label together with the coordinate type of that label's layout.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellInde.text: The exact tagged sum places resolved-mode coordinates and complex ports first, followed by two k-coordinate blocks for the actuator and pin variables.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellCalc.text: The record joins mode layouts, leaf coefficients, model splits, local forms, port identifiers, surrogate pairings and trace-credit ownership for every cell.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylRadiu.text: Returns r from the first two Cartesian coordinates, leaving the height coordinate out of the norm.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylHeigh.text: Returns the signed height z; reflection to the stored upper half-plane is performed separately.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.cylPoint.text: Builds the Cartesian point with radius r, angle θ and height z. Here θ is the spatial angle, whereas the paper uses θ for time and φ for angle.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.radialUn.text: The first vector of the moving cylindrical frame is represented in the fixed Cartesian basis.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.angularU.text: The second frame vector differentiates the radial direction with respect to angle and is orthogonal to it.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.axialUni.text: The third frame vector is the constant unit vector in the height direction.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.azimuth.text: Multiplies an integer mode by the azimuthal order. This one-frequency helper is distinct from the active two-integer label map of (B.2).

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox.text: Stores the four endpoints of a rectangle Q in the nonnegative meridian quadrant. Endpoint ordering is not part of the data record and is imposed by IsCellBox.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox..text: An axis cell is recognised by the exact equality r₁=0, rather than a numerical tolerance.
The stored meridian rectangle includes all four sides. Later integration permits shared boundaries of measure zero.
A cell describes all angles and both signs of height because membership uses the absolute value of z.
Axis cells use radial weight r, whereas off-axis cells use weight one. This is the Jacobi versus Legendre distinction in (B.27).
Maps the radial interval affinely to the reference interval from minus one to one. A valid cell supplies the nonzero denominator.
Maps the height interval affinely to the same reference interval; its orientation follows the ordered cell endpoints.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBo.text: Requires nonnegative lower endpoints and strictly positive width and height. These inequalities justify the affine reference coordinates and exclude degenerate rectangles.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox..text: The factor is one for axis cells and r₁ otherwise, matching the exceptional convention in (B.27).
Takes a one-variable derivative while holding the height fixed. It is an evaluator, so differentiability must be established separately.
Takes a one-variable derivative while holding the radius fixed. This complex-valued derivative is used before the finite matrix forms are assembled.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.text: Stores per-cell resolved, tested and eliminated harmonics and their degree choices. The geometry and set relations are validated by IsCellMesh and later layout predicates.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.closedHalfPl.text: The mesh is described in the nonnegative r,z quadrant, including the axis and the symmetry plane.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.region.text: Forms the union over the finite cell index. An empty mesh therefore has an empty region at this definition alone.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.exterior.text: Subtracts the cell union from the closed quadrant. Later estimates restrict the corresponding integrals to the open quarter-plane.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMesh.maxVolumeDeg.text: Takes the finite supremum of the per-label volume degrees. On an empty resolved set the natural-number supremum is zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.IsCellMesh.text: Checks nondegenerate cells, negligible overlaps, harmonic-set relations and basic degree bounds. Its skeleton lower bound is −1; the full layout condition later strengthens that to at least one on resolved modes.

Breakdown.CertCell.halfPlane.text: The analytic integrals use r>0 and z>0. The finite rectangles include their boundaries, whose contribution is handled by measure-zero statements.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.CreditPatch.re.text: The patch uses the radial interval from inner to outer and the height interval from zero to height, adjacent to the reflection plane.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownSolid.text: The set keeps points in the chosen solid with r>0 and excludes points belonging to any other cell, removing shared faces from these pointwise split bounds.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPressu.text: The segmentation covers every non-axis boundary side with disjoint interiors, correct opposite-side coordinates and orthonormal trace tests. Each conjunction remains an independent obligation.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPlaneM.text: Every side and pressure-side segment at z=0 must find an identical segment and test-coefficient function in the reflected layout. The displayed predicate is directional.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ActuatorSu.text: Binds each forcing field bᵢ to its compact shape data and asks the cells to cover a square containing its support. The support radius H is an existential real, with no sign condition in this structure.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.ChartPara.text: Stores the radius scale L and auxiliary core, regularity and azimuthal parameters for the field construction. Positivity belongs to IsChartParams.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.IsChartPa.text: Requires positive L, core radius and auxiliary epsilon, epsilon below one eighth, and positive azimuthal order. The active cell premise later requires the stronger order bound κ≥3.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightRat.text: This is η=z/|y| in (B.3), with Lean's total value zero at the origin. Origin regularity is supplied by the field-shape conditions.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.qOf.text: Computes 1−η², the factor that controls behaviour at the axis in (B.7) and (B.8).

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.chartT.text: This is σ=|y|/(|y|+L) in the paper. The Lean name t does not denote the time variable here.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.radialVec.text: Represents y/|y| componentwise and uses the total value zero at y=0. The complete field needs the prescribed vanishing factors at the origin.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.polarVecQ.text: Represents the paper's vector p, including the factor that removes the unit polar vector's axis singularity.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.azimVecQ.text: Represents the paper's vector a, using Cartesian coordinates divided by |y| and vanishing at the axis away from the origin.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.TensorMes.text: Stores separate radial-chart and nonnegative-height knot lists. No ordering, endpoint or nonemptiness proof is included in the data record.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.IsTensorM.text: Requires strictly increasing knot lists, each beginning at zero and ending at one. These facts provide at least one interval in each direction.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.cellIndex.text: Counts internal knots at or below the evaluation point, so an interior knot selects the piece on its right. Values outside the chart range are still defined.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.cellCount.text: Uses list length minus one with natural-number subtraction. Mesh validity is needed to rule out malformed short lists.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.text: A spline supplies a polynomial for every pair of natural indices. A finite serialisation must specify values outside the valid rectangle indices.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.ev.text: Evaluates the polynomial selected by the two knot lists. The definition contains no interpolation or continuity check; join predicates establish those properties.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.atFirst.text: Replaces the first polynomial variable by a complex constant while leaving the second variable unchanged.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.atSecond.text: Replaces the second polynomial variable while preserving the first. This is used in exact polynomial join identities.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.tDeriv.text: Iterates formal differentiation in the first variable. Order zero leaves the polynomial unchanged.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.xDeriv.text: Iterates formal differentiation in the second variable, which represents the chart height rather than a Cartesian coordinate.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.co.text: Keeps the mesh and conjugates each polynomial coefficient. This is the coefficient-level operation used for harmonic reality conditions.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.Spline.Va.text: Quantifies over all natural indices, using one as the default radial knot. Thus a cutoff below one also constrains out-of-range pieces, not only the serialised valid cells.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.weightPol.text: Forms σ^e₀(1−σ)^e₁, the origin and infinity factors used in the field formulas. The exponents are natural numbers.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.radialSca.text: Applies σ(1−σ)∂σ, corresponding to |y|∂|y| in (B.3). Radial phase terms are added by later operators.

Breakdown.CellCert.GivenFields.heightDer.text: Differentiates the chart coefficient in η while fixing σ. This is separate from the physical height derivative in cylindrical coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar.text: Stores separate upper and lower spline functions and a natural decay exponent. Each half is evaluated in nonnegative chart height.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ChartScalar..text: Multiplies the selected half-chart spline's real part by (1−σ)^decay and uses the upper chart on the symmetry plane.
Swaps upper and lower splines while keeping the decay exponent. The symmetry conditions later compare this reflected data with its partner.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.SplineJoins.text: Requires a valid tensor mesh and exact identities of derivatives through the selected order at every internal knot. The two directions have separate interval guards.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsJoinedScal.text: Combines joins on both halves, a shared radial knot list and signed derivative matching at η=0. The factor (−1)^o accounts for reflection of the lower chart.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsConstantCo.text: Requires a positive cutoff that is a stored upper radial knot and one complex constant for all pieces below it on both halves. These outer requirements remain mandatory even if an inner index range were empty.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsFlatAtOrig.text: Requires one common complex value at the first radial face of all upper and lower height pieces. It fixes values at the origin boundary, not every derivative there.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.HasNonnegVal.text: Requires the real parts of both spline evaluations to be nonnegative at every point of the unit square. Coefficient positivity is a possible sufficient proof route, not the literal predicate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.text: Stores real tables on a common tensor mesh and an integer decay power. Negative powers are allowed by the data type, unlike ChartScalar's natural exponent.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsFullMesh.text: The two strictly ordered breakpoint lists cover σ∈[0,1] and η∈[−1,1]. This differs from the half-height mesh used for scalar weights.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJoinedSp.text: The σ and η joining orders are independent. Equality is of whole restricted polynomials along each interface, rather than equality at sampled interface points.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectPol.text: Substitution leaves σ unchanged and replaces η by −η; any overall odd sign is applied by reflectSpline.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reflectSpl.text: The height breakpoints are negated and reversed, cell indices are reversed, and odd fields gain a minus sign.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.SplineAgre.text: Agreement requires identical meshes and equal polynomials on every active cell. It does not require equality of the total piece functions at unused indices.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.KeyAmp.con.text: Conjugation acts on all four splines and γ, while the origin and decay exponents remain fixed.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.KeyAmp.ref.text: A is even under η-reflection and B, S and T are odd; the stored γ and exponents are retained.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetDof.text: A degree of freedom is either a derivative order at a breakpoint or an interior bubble index on one interval. Constructor indices are natural numbers and are not intrinsically range checked.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.text: The interpolation depth D controls endpoint derivatives through order D−1; bubbleCount supplies the additional interval coefficients.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.jetUnit.text: The polynomial normalizes the selected endpoint derivative with 1/p! and enforces the required vanishing at the opposite endpoint.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalLeft.text: The affine pullback and the factor (b−a)^p turn the unit Hermite jet into a physical derivative at the left endpoint.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.nodalRight.text: The reflected affine coordinate and the factor (a−b)^p preserve the physical derivative convention at the right endpoint.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.bubblePoly.text: The factors at a and b vanish to depth D at both endpoints; a midpoint monomial distinguishes the extra interior coefficients.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.text: A coordinate contributes only to its adjacent nodal interval or its own bubble interval, and out-of-range derivative or bubble orders contribute zero.
The active set contains every endpoint derivative below depth D and every prescribed bubble on each interval.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.re.text: A node k is sent to the opposite node and an interval i to the opposite interval; derivative and bubble orders are retained.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetAxis.do.text: The reflection sign is (−1)^p for a pth derivative and (−1)^s for a midpoint bubble of order s.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetAxis.text: Strict knot order, the specified endpoints and positive depth are required. Nonzero gaps follow on active intervals from these conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsSymmetri.text: Negating and reversing the breakpoint list must reproduce the same list, which allows reflection to stay on one stored height mesh.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetSpline.text: The coefficient function has two JetDof arguments, one for σ and one for η, even though evaluation uses finite active subsets.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.embedFirst.text: The univariate polynomial is evaluated at the first variable of the bivariate polynomial ring.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.embedSecon.text: The univariate polynomial is evaluated at the second variable of the bivariate polynomial ring.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetSpline..text: Every cell polynomial is assembled from the tensor product of the two active jet bases and their complex coefficients.
For every radial coordinate and active height coordinate, the reflected coefficient equals the prescribed parity times the derivative/bubble reflection sign.
A fixed conjugate-reflection orbit imposes conjugation in addition to the height reflection sign and component parity.
The value jet at the first radial node vanishes for every height coordinate, including coordinates outside the active evaluation set.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.OriginProf.text: The function g is a polynomial up to σg and a constant afterwards; its normalization supplies the controlled linear term at y=0.
The polynomial branch includes the joining point σg. Conditions on its derivatives supply agreement with the constant tail.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsOriginPr.text: The polynomial is normalized by g(0)=1 and joins its constant tail through order two when σg<1. At σg=1 no tail join inside the compactified domain is needed.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartCoord.text: The map |y|/(|y|+L) sends finite radii to [0,1) once L>0 is known.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.chartRadiu.text: The inverse chart is Lσ/(1−σ) on σ<1. Lean also gives a total value at σ=1, so that endpoint is not a representation of infinity.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.phaseSlope.text: This is 2|y|²f′(|y|²), expressed through the inverse radial chart, before multiplication by the integer l.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shiftedSca.text: The operator Vl adds i l times the radial-phase derivative factor to σ(1−σ)∂σ.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.polarFacto.text: The factor 1−η² appears in the stream-function divergence identity and vanishes at both ends of the height chart.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.axisFactor.text: The factor (1−η²)² supplies the stronger axis vanishing of the nonzero-azimuthal branch in (B.7).

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.streamValu.text: The stream function is γg(σ)η plus the spline S; γ is retained separately so that the origin gradient is controlled explicitly.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.reducedCom.text: The definition branches on ι₁=0 and implements the two constructions (B.7) and (B.8). Its third component in the nonzero branch divides by κι₁.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsTimeFiel.text: This record ties the branch-specific joining orders, origin conditions, decay exponents and conjugation/reflection identities to one harmonic field.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsCompactT.text: The active splines vanish from a cutoff σb<1 and have a suitable interior breakpoint; the γ term is zero for the axisymmetric branch.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetKeyData.text: The four amplitude splines are held in jet coordinates, while γ and the two vanishing/decay exponents are stored directly.
Each jet spline is converted to cell polynomials; γ and the exponent data are copied unchanged.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.GivenJetDa.text: Only selected orbit representatives are stored. The full field is obtained by the conjugation/reflection closure.
The representative jets become amplitudes and are extended to the full symmetry-closed key set.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.JetSpline..text: Every coefficient equals its complex conjugate. The quantification covers all two-index jet coordinates, including unused ones.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsJetClass.text: The radial and height axes have their prescribed full domains, and each depth exceeds the required joining order by at least one.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsGivenJet.text: One representative is allowed per symmetry orbit, with additional parity and real/conjugate-reflection constraints on stabilised orbits. Joining depths and origin vanishing encode the field conditions before interpolation.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.mo.text: Only f is changed, by a scalar multiple of f_*; the chart length, symmetry order and origin profile are retained.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ph.text: The sum k·α selects the amount of radial-phase motion in (B.9).

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.wi.text: The constructor allows W⁰ and each tangent Wⁱ to have their own g while retaining the common chart and phase.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.af.text: The centre plus ΣαᵢWⁱ is affine for fixed shape parameters; evaluating it at paramsAt α also introduces the moving radial phase.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.St.text: The piecewise polynomial χ is stored by a breakpoint list and a total function from interval indices to polynomials.
Evaluation selects a polynomial with the shared cellIndex convention, including that convention's behaviour at endpoints.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is.text: The profile is C² across active knots, vanishes up to an interior breakpoint σχ and equals one on a neighbourhood of 1.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.st.text: The integral of χ(r/(r+L))/r up to √s is f_*(s); the zero core removes the apparent singularity at r=0 on the valid route.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr.text: This specialises the radial step integral to the profile's chart length and stored χ.
The radius Lσχ/(1−σχ) bounds the region where f_* vanishes and the profile depends affinely on α through amplitudes alone.
The radial phase becomes f+(k·α)f_*, while the other shape parameters remain unchanged.
The centre and tangent fields are combined using the phase chosen at the same α, so the full spatial field is not globally affine in α.
The spline amplitude is multiplied by separate powers at σ=0, σ=1 and η=±1; these exponents control the pressure's regularity and decay.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.pr.text: The term is Eι,l σ^h₀(1−σ)^h(1−η²)^h′₀ times the stored scalar spline.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.sh.text: The scalar correction q is the real part of a finite harmonic sum; the physical pressure gradient later subtracts |Wᵃ|²/2.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is.text: Conjugation/reflection, continuity, decay h≥2 and the branch-specific axis/origin clauses are required. In the nonzero-azimuthal branch, origin regularity allows either a positive radial power or exact vanishing.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Pr.text: The field q⁰+Σαᵢqⁱ is evaluated with the same moving phase as the approximate velocity profile.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.pr.text: The centre amplitude data are evaluated with fα and their own g, retaining α-dependence through the phase.

Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.planeOf.text: The map keeps signed z and nonnegative cylindrical radius, so reflection of knots must be handled explicitly.

Breakdown.CertCell.KnotZero.zeroOn.text: The Hessian is replaced by zero at points whose cylindrical pair lies in the selected planar set; equality away from that set is literal.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.planeNorm.text: This is √(r²+z²), used to recognise compactified-radius spheres in the meridian plane.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.sphereKnot.text: Each stored radial breakpoint contributes the equation |(r,z)|=Lσ/(1−σ). The endpoint σ=1 has a totalized Lean value and must not be treated numerically as an infinite radius.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.coneKnots.text: Each height breakpoint η contributes the cone equation z=η√(r²+z²).

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.splineKnot.text: The planar exceptional set is the union of its radial spheres and height cones.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyKnots.text: The exceptional set includes knots from all four stored amplitude splines, even if the field formula uses only one branch for that key.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeKnots.text: The set includes the axis, reflection plane, origin, the g-joining sphere and every active amplitude's partition knots.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.mirrorKnot.text: Both a point and its z-reflection are tested against the shape-knot set, making the exceptional set compatible with the spatial symmetry.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.knotZeroHe.text: The reference Hessian is exactly zero on the reflection-closed knot set and equals the harmonic Hessian elsewhere; the weak-Hessian route accounts for this null-set convention.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetA.text: The axis adds a node-scale list and bubble-normalisation list to the ordinary jet-axis data. Their default values and zero behaviour are part of decoding.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.symmetricJ.text: The finite binomial sum fixes the normalization of Pⱼ^(α,α); this exact normalization is used in the scaled bubble conversion.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetA.text: The breakpoints, depth and number of bubbles are retained while scaling and normalisation data are forgotten.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasSymmetr.text: Only the scale-list length and reversal symmetry are asserted here. Positivity or nonzero values are not part of this predicate.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetS.text: The coefficient array is stored with two scaled axes; evaluation requires the basis conversion to ordinary JetSpline coordinates.
This helper attaches the unchanged coefficient function to the unscaled axes so that algebraic symmetry conditions can be checked before conversion.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledKeyD.text: The four scalar amplitudes use scaled jet splines while γ and the radial exponents are stored directly.
This coefficient-view helper applies coefValues to all four amplitudes without performing the scaling transformation.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ScaledJetD.text: The finite representative key set is paired with a total function supplying scaled amplitude records.
The helper exposes unconverted coefficient values so that IsGivenJetData can check orbit and parity identities on the stored coordinates.
Each representative is converted to ordinary jets before model closes the keys under their symmetries.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsScaledJe.text: The unconverted coefficient view must satisfy the jet-data conditions; symmetric height scales are additionally required on the relevant fixed orbits.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.HasEdgeBre.text: Requires the chosen support boundary to occur in both amplitudes used by each field key, choosing the nonzero-azimuthal or axisymmetric representation as appropriate.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelTime.text: Maps the lattice label ι to 2ι₂−ι₁, the integer multiplying 2π times the period-one time variable in (B.2).

Breakdown.CertCell.labelAzimuth.text: Maps ι to κι₁, the integer multiplying the spatial angle in (B.2).

Breakdown.CertCell.labelHarmonic.text: Combines the temporal and azimuthal integers for use with the imported mode operators. It preserves the distinction between lattice labels and frequency pairs.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelFlip.text: Implements ι↦(−ι₁,ι₂−ι₁), which reverses the angular frequency and preserves the time frequency.

Breakdown.CertCell.flipLabel.text: Reverses the second coordinate of a frequency pair. Its input is already a temporal-angular frequency pair, unlike labelFlip's lattice label.

Breakdown.CertCell.IsLatticeHarmonic.text: Asserts that a frequency pair is the image of some lattice label. Injectivity of the label map needs a positive azimuthal order.

Breakdown.CertCell.planePoint.text: Embeds a meridian point in space at angle zero, where the reduced mode densities are evaluated.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelVel.text: Uses the frequency pair of ι and evaluates the mode at time zero and angle zero. This is a spatial component array of the mode in (B.12).

Breakdown.CertCell.labelGrad.text: Reads the corresponding gradient mode as a pair-indexed complex array, retaining the order of output and derivative indices.

Breakdown.CertCell.flipPoint.text: Implements rotation by π about the first Cartesian axis, sending (y₁,y₂,y₃) to (y₁,−y₂,−y₃).

Breakdown.CertCell.frameSign.text: The radial component has sign +1 and the angular and axial components have sign −1 under the stored half-plane reflection.

Breakdown.CertCell.frameUnit.text: Lists the radial, angular and axial vectors in component order. Matrix fields use the same order for both indices.

Breakdown.CertCell.pointAngle.text: Uses the complex argument of y₁+i y₂. Its branch convention is harmless only together with the periodic harmonic and axis regularity conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.pointPlane.text: Returns (r,z), before the negative-height branch reflects z to the stored upper half-plane.

Breakdown.CertCell.labelPhase.text: Evaluates Eι from (B.2). The variable σ here denotes period-one time, unlike the paper's compactified radial σ in (B.3).

Breakdown.CertCell.labelValueAt.text: For negative height, switches to labelFlip and multiplies by the supplied frame sign before evaluating at positive height. This is distinct from complex conjugation under label negation.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.planeVal.text: Uses the component's reflection sign and the flipped label on negative height, while keeping upper-plane coefficients unchanged.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.field.text: Sums real harmonic contributions in the moving frame over every cell indicator. Shared cell boundaries may receive more than one contribution; the integral theory uses negligible overlaps.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellVecField.IsConjug.text: Requires label closure under negation and flip and conjugate evaluated polynomials under negation. The polynomial equality quantifies over every label, not just labels in the finite set.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.planeVal.text: The reflection sign is the product of the two frame signs, reversing the entries with exactly one radial index.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.frameMap.text: Maps column component b to row component a through frame vectors, giving a continuous linear map in Cartesian space. This fixes the gradient-index convention.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.field.text: Sums the real harmonic coefficient matrices after conversion to the moving frame, with a separate indicator for each cell solid.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellMatField.IsConjug.text: Requires finite labels closed under negation and flip, and conjugate polynomial values for every label and component pair. It does not by itself identify the matrix field as a derivative.

Breakdown.CertCell.rowPartFactor.text: Multiplication by −i makes the real part of a complex field equal its imaginary part. The true branch retains its real part.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsActuatorIn.text: A single j_* rectangle contains each forcing-field label, and every label in that rectangle must avoid every λ- and μ-piece on K.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.GeneratedByC.text: Each declared symmetry must be a nonnegative integral power of the half-period rotation, optionally followed by the spatial flip, with an additional integer time shift.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.text: The key is the pair (ι,l) in Eι,l: its lattice label determines the time and azimuthal frequencies, while phaseIndex is the separate radial-phase integer.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.n.text: Complex conjugation negates both the lattice label ι and the radial-phase integer l.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.FieldKey.f.text: The spatial flip maps ι to ι♭ and leaves l unchanged because the radial phase depends only on |y|².

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyPhase.text: Eι,l combines normalized time frequency 2ι₂−ι₁, azimuthal frequency κι₁ and radial phase l f(|y|²).

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.keyVector.text: The three reduced components multiply y/|y|, p and a from (B.4), and the result is multiplied by Eι,l.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.complexFie.text: The finite sum is formed before taking real parts, preserving the conjugate-pair construction of (B.6).

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.shapeInfoF.text: The decoded real field is the real part of the finite complex harmonic sum, with normalized time as its first argument.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.harmonicsO.text: The image converts each stored lattice label to its actual time and azimuthal frequencies; radial-phase indices do not create additional time/angular labels.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.labelsOf.text: The image forgets the radial-phase integer but retains the paper's lattice label ι. It is different from the physical-frequency image harmonicsOf.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.orbitClosu.text: The finite key set is enlarged by conjugation, reflection and their composition, retaining duplicates only once as a Finset.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.closureAmp.text: The constructor prefers a directly stored representative, then its conjugate, then its reflection, then the combined transform. Representative uniqueness and fixed-orbit conditions make these choices consistent.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.closureDat.text: The orbit-closed keys and their transformed amplitudes form the full TimeFieldData object used for evaluation.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.axisRotation.text: The coordinate formula supplies the exact rotations under which each amplitude has one azimuthal wave number.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.complexComponent.text: Components 0 and 1 are R₁+iR₂ and R₁−iR₂; component 2 is R₃. These are scalar wave channels, not cylindrical vector components.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.componentWeight.text: The two circular components each receive weight 1/2 and the vertical component receives weight 1 in the squared norm.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.gradAt.text: The wrapper extracts the (a,b) cylindrical-frame entry of the label's gradient mode at a meridian point.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.velAt.text: The wrapper extracts one cylindrical-frame component of the label's vector mode at a meridian point.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellMode.text: The test uses only |ι₁|≤cut, so it is an azimuthal label cutoff and does not bound the temporal index ι₂.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.up.text: The upper table is selected at the compactified radius σ and the signed height ratio η; the radial decay factor is applied by eval.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.lo.text: The lower table uses −η, so both half-space tables are indexed by a nonnegative height coordinate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.ev.text: The decoded weight is the selected table value times (1−σ) to an integer exponent; points on y₃=0 select the upper table.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.StepDatum.mi.text: Reflection exchanges the upper and lower tables while retaining their common mesh and decay exponent.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsPositiveSt.text: A valid tensor mesh is required independently of the positivity conditions on its active cells. Positivity concerns both half-space tables.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven.text: Lean calls the paper's λ-pieces eps-pieces; this record stores the scalar functions before the rotating frame and transport bound are supplied.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven.text: The μ-piece stores one mode set, a decaying weight, two positive auxiliary step functions and a scalar for the Young bounds. Its eta field is that balancing constant, distinct from the height coordinate η.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.EpsGiven.mir.text: The mode set is mapped by the harmonic reflection, while all spatial scalar tables exchange their two half-spaces.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.MuGiven.mirr.text: Reflection acts on the mode set and scalar tables; the auxiliary number η is unchanged.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.WeightValues.text: This record packages the class weights Dι and Zι together with the λ- and μ-pieces in their chart representation. Frame rates and transport bounds are attached later.
The constructor evaluates each stored scalar in the chart and adds the supplied rotation rate and transport-bound function.
The constructor evaluates the stored μ-weight and auxiliary steps while preserving its harmonic set and scalar η.
The class map and constants are retained, while the scalar records become the function-valued PieceWeights used by the coercive form.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsWeightValu.text: The record imposes the specified joining orders, origin behaviour, decay powers and positive auxiliary functions. Only the strain class weight Dι is required to be nonnegative here; Zι has different conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsFlipClosed.text: The supplied permutations of λ- and μ-indices implement reflection, and the class weights agree after both label and spatial reflection.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsWeightInst.text: The function-valued weights are identified with the decoded scalar representation for every α in K. The frame-reflection equalities are quantified over every parameter vector, without a K guard.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsRadialPh.text: The phase f has a C³ extension to an open interval containing [0,∞), together with bounds for ρf′, ρ²f″ and ρ³f‴. A function field alone does not establish these analytic properties.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsShapePar.text: The formal constructor requires L>0 and κ>0, plus the phase and origin-profile conditions. The paper's overall symmetry setup also specifies κ≥3 elsewhere.

Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.Enclosu.text: The inequalities are uniform in time, space, rotations and the relevant harmonics. They include the transport bounds, a positive one-sided frequency margin and the three shared enclosure constants.

Breakdown.CertCell.InstanceSplit.ValuesF.text: Amplitude and supremum bounds are invariant under axial rotations and compatible with label/spatial reflection; the transport-bound functions are axisymmetric.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.ShapeValue.text: The seven fields give positive period and weight, a constant weight function, and harmonic support closed under negation and reflection and containing zero and the given labels.

Breakdown.CertCell.ScalarShape.planeMinE.text: At y₃=0 the minimum of the upper and lower tables is used, unlike ordinary StepDatum.eval. Away from the plane it selects the corresponding half-space table.

Breakdown.CertCell.ScalarShape.ChartBoun.text: The enclosure includes an integer power of σ, a decaying step datum and a separately specified value at the origin.
The origin is handled before the possibly negative σ power is evaluated; elsewhere the reflection-plane minimum is multiplied by σ to the stored power.

Breakdown.CertCell.ScalarShape.BoundValu.text: The record stores the four per-harmonic envelopes and the two global vorticity envelopes in one radial chart.
The finite support is retained and each scalar chart datum becomes the corresponding function in HarmonicBounds.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.BoundValue.text: Per-parameter harmonic bounds and the transport bounds are represented separately, allowing the latter to share a single speed chart.

Breakdown.CertCell.GivenShape.IsBoundVal.text: These are equalities of complete bound records and functions on the parameter set, rather than numerical upper-bound tests at selected points.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.ampOf.text: The index order is velocity, velocity gradient, vorticity and vorticity gradient, matching the four envelopes used in the multiplier errors.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsPeriod.text: The stored periodInverse approximates 1/S(α), not S(α), and its error bound must hold for every α in K.

Breakdown.CertCell.IsBoxUniform.text: Keeps the reference model and coefficient bounds independent of α. The eps and mu pieces are compared after setting their frame fields to zero, leaving exactly that frame dependence exempt.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.generator.text: Places the selected test on its cell and original label and uses the reflection machinery to define negative-height values. The realPart flag chooses the real or imaginary component.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.generatorFi.text: Evaluates the selected cellwise polynomial generator with the global azimuthal order and the cell boxes.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.testValue.text: Reads the cell, label and test number stored for that row, then evaluates its chosen component in the cell's reference coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.fieldPairin.text: Uses the full period-space pairing of the real generators. This matrix includes the real/imaginary and reflection conventions of the generator construction.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.mix.text: Uses the functional calculus inverse square root when the Gram matrix is Hermitian, and zero otherwise. The positive-definiteness proof supplies the intended orthogonalisation behaviour.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowFieldOf.text: Mixes the real generators by the inverse-square-root matrix. The paper's row weight is stored separately in rowWeightOf, so this field alone does not include its square-root weight.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.rowWeightOf.text: Divides the cell-label test weight by coercivity. IsRowInstance requires positive coercivity before this is used in the certificate.

Breakdown.CertCell.RowValues.testBlockMa.text: Integrates r times each test component product with conjugation on the first index. Positive definiteness is checked for each tested cell-label block.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowValues.text: Checks the finite row indexing, conjugate representatives, real zero mode, complete tests, divergence, axis behaviour and positive-definite block Grams. These conditions justify the global Gram orthogonalisation.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsRowInstanc.text: Identifies the certificate's rows and weights with the constructed orthonormal rows and scaled weights, with positive coercivity and the required global row bound.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.ActuatorShap.text: The fields bᵢ carry explicit measurability, weak-gradient and period-one conditions. Mode support is stated away from the axis, while the two discrete symmetries hold almost everywhere.

Breakdown.CertCell.Instance.IsPinInstanc.text: The analytic pin field is exactly the polynomial field decoded from the cells, and each cell representation has the required conjugate closure.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.CylModeData.text: Stores a finite harmonic support and three cylindrical jet amplitudes per label. The field decoder supplies an extra radial factor.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.cylField.text: Combines each harmonic phase with r times its spline amplitude and the rotating cylindrical frame vector. Taking real parts yields the real field Φ_l.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.VanishesBeyond.text: Requires radial and polar node or bubble coefficients beyond the chosen support radius to vanish, with quantifiers over all natural indices. Missing breakpoints are read as the support radius itself.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsCylModeData.text: Separates a positive support radius from a larger mesh radius and requires support boundaries to be actual spline knots. All active harmonic amplitudes obey the coefficient vanishing predicate.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.PinShapeEntry.text: Stores both the cylindrical pin potentials Φ_l and compact generators Φ̃_l, together with the cell matrix fields used by the certificate. A later equality ties these representations together.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.PinShapeEntry.p.text: Constructs the PinData pair by decoding the cylindrical Φ_l fields and the compact Φ̃_l generator fields.
Reads the stored piecewise pin matrix using the entry’s own mesh and rotational order. Equality with the certificate’s pinField is required separately.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPinShapeEntry.text: Checks mesh geometry, compact cylindrical supports and compact generator data with support knots. It does not itself identify the resulting pin matrix field with the certificate’s field.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.secondDeriv.text: The Hessian is an iterated Fréchet derivative, whose trace supplies the Laplacian in the residual formula.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.matrixDivergence.text: The contraction differentiates K along each coordinate vector and then applies the resulting linear map to that same vector. Compare this convention before matching the paper's div Fᵀ notation.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.transposeApply.text: The component formula computes Kᵀz for a real linear map K, as required by the adjoint transport term.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.timeDerivative.text: The derivative is in the period-one variable θ; the reciprocal physical period is supplied separately by adjointTransport.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.advectionShift.text: The expression (∇δ)ᵀζ−(δ·∇)ζ is the formal adjoint contribution of the linearized advection.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.adjointTransport.text: The time term uses −1/P, and the dilation adjoint contributes −ζ−(y·∇)ζ/2 before the advection difference.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialData.text: The names theta, phi, flux and pressure correspond to Gⱼ, Uⱼ, the matrix potential and qⱼ, with matrix conventions fixed by matrixDivergence.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.remainderField.text: The residual combines the transport field, the pin-flux divergence, ∇q, ∆G, w_*∆U and the matrix-potential divergence in the source's linear-map convention.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialNumbers.text: The numbers bound Gⱼ, ∇Uⱼ, Fⱼ and the remaining dual norm separately, before they are combined in (B.53).

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.potentialDefect.text: The bound is the square root of n_G²+(w_*n_U+n_F+n_R)²/w_*, matching the first term of (B.53).

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PotentialNorms.text: The three L² inequalities are period integrals and all four stored numbers are nonnegative. The remainder bound is imposed separately on the actual residual.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.RemainderBounded.text: The squared weighted norm is bounded by (ρ/2)², encoding the factor 2 in the Hardy estimate. Measurability and ρ≥0 are explicit.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AzimuthalBounded.text: The expansion has distinct (component,time-frequency,azimuthal-order) triples, measurable amplitudes and an almost-everywhere spatial identity at every time. Its squared weight is (|m|+1/2)⁻² with circular-component weights.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.DualBounded.text: One shared decomposition R=R₁+R₂ assigns an azimuthal bound to R₁ and a Hardy bound to R₂, with the two nonnegative bounds summing to at most ρ.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.PinData.text: The potential fields encode Φₗ and the solenoidal generators encode Φ̃ₗ, whose difference is charged separately in (B.53).

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectEnt.text: This generic record allows some parameter directions to have fitted potential certificates and the rest to use weighted norm bounds. The specialised cell route later forces fittedSet to be empty.
The pin correction uses the antisymmetric part ∇Φ̃−(∇Φ̃)ᵀ inside the flux, so expanding its divergence requires the generator's divergence-free property.
The centre field may depend on α through the moving phase, although the central reciprocal period remains fixed.
The directional correction combines adjoint advection by the fitted field with the negative time derivative weighted by the reciprocal-period rate.

Fitted directions contribute coordinate bounds times potential defects; complementary directions use weighted Cauchy–Schwarz and the period-rate sum. For the cell route the fitted contribution is zero by AdjointEntryLinks.
The pin error contributes n_Φ directly, while the pin-coefficient norm multiplies the gradient approximation error and divides by √w_*.

Breakdown.AdjointDefect.AdjointDefectBou.text: The conditions quantify uniformly over α∈K and retain shared witnesses for the free-direction dual bounds. Their final sum is compared with the certificate's aⱼ.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ba.text: The pairing integrates over one normalized period and the closed ball of radius rχ. This convention differs from the paper's open-ball notation only at the sphere when integrability is available.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ti.text: This derivative is taken before the reciprocal period is inserted in the residual coefficients of (B.57).

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.ce.text: F⁽⁰⁾ includes the similarity drift, Laplacian, convection, central force and ∇(q⁰−|W⁰|²/2) in one explicit formula.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.li.text: F⁽ⁱ⁾ includes both reciprocal-period contributions, both cross-advection terms and the gradient correction −∇(W⁰·Wⁱ).

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.qu.text: This is one ordered contribution in the αᵢαₗ expansion; off-diagonal coefficients later add the term with i and l exchanged.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Of.text: The record stores affine reciprocal-period/force coefficients, numerical centre/linear/quadratic pairings with their errors, and two far-field norm bounds.
The centre coefficient is evaluated with the original phase f and centre origin profile, appropriate to the ball where f_* vanishes.
The tangent coefficient uses its own origin profile, the original phase and the corresponding pressure and force tangent.
The first index supplies the reciprocal-period rate and advecting tangent, while the second supplies the differentiated tangent.
Diagonal coefficients use one ordered term; off-diagonal coefficients use both orders and are counted once in the upper-triangular sum.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.co.text: Box coordinates use their explicit radius; complementary ellipsoid coordinates use |R|/|sᵢ|, whose interpretation requires nonzero scales on the valid certificate route.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.of.text: The sum subtracts the diagonal scale in the linear term, counts each quadratic pair with i≤l once, and adds the exterior product bound.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Is.text: The period and multiplier are affine on K, the core pairings have certified errors, and the outside norms are uniform on K. The resulting offset equals the constructed sum exactly.

Breakdown.CellReduction.Instantiation.Ad.text: The record identifies the adjoint field, constant pin coefficients, moved centre/tangent fields and period rates. It also makes every fitted direction set empty on this route.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent.text: Uses the x+iy, x−iy and axial components so that each has one azimuthal phase shift. This is the component encoding of the potential fields.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent.sh.text: Adds +1 for x+iy, −1 for x−iy, and zero for the axial component to the harmonic’s azimuthal frequency.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotComponent.ca.text: The two horizontal complex components receive a polar-sine factor; the axial component does not.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotScalar.text: A tensor-product Hermite amplitude is multiplied by explicit near-origin, far-field and axis factors. Endpoint vanishing may supply part of the required radial order.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.polarSine.text: Computes √(1−η²) using the height ratio defined on Cartesian points. Its values at the origin and axis follow the existing totalized chart conventions.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.scalarValue.text: Combines time, azimuthal and radial phases with radial weights, axis factors and the spline value. The optional polar sine is separate from the integer axis power.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.componentValue.text: Supplies the component-specific azimuthal shift and polar-sine choice to the scalar potential decoder.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.coordsOfCompone.text: Recovers x and y from x+iy and x−iy using factors 1/2 and 1/(2i), while leaving the axial component unchanged.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotKeyData.text: Stores amplitudes for G_j, U_j, the radial and polar contributions to F_j, and q_j. The radial/polar flux entries encode vector components of matrix columns.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotentialSeries.text: Stores a finite key set and a total key-to-amplitude function. Only amplitudes at keys in the finite set enter the decoded field.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.vectorPotential.text: Sums the selected complex components, reconstructs Cartesian coordinates and takes the real vector. The selector chooses the G or U amplitude family.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxVector.text: Forms a vector in the input index by combining the radial direction with the polar vector, for one output component and harmonic key.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxEntry.text: Sums the flux modes, reconstructs the output component and takes its real part. The two indices are output component a and input direction i.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.fluxMap.text: Turns the output-by-input matrix into a continuous linear map. Relative to the paper’s derivative convention this represents the transposed flux used in div F_jᵀ.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.pressureValue.text: Uses the unshifted harmonic azimuth, with no extra polar-sine factor, and takes the real part of the scalar sum.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.PotentialSeries.text: Packages the decoded G, U, flux and pressure functions into the adjoint-potential interface. This data conversion contains no proof of regularity.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsJetMesh.text: Requires strictly ordered breaks with specified endpoints. It intentionally omits the stronger joining conditions of IsJetAxis, allowing the tangential discontinuities permitted in the flux representation.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.StartVanishOrde.text: Requires all node-jet coefficients below the requested order to vanish at the first radial breakpoint, for every polar degree of freedom.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.EndVanishOrder.text: Requires the low-order radial node coefficients to vanish at the final compactified breakpoint, with the final index computed by cellCount.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.dofMeetsEndCell.text: Classifies node and bubble degrees of freedom that can affect the first or last cell. Natural subtraction in N−1 is truncated at zero.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.AxisCellsVanish.text: Requires zero coefficients for every polar degree of freedom that touches either polar endpoint cell. This supplies an alternative to an explicit positive axis power.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.StartRowConstan.text: Zeros all non-value polar degrees of freedom in the initial radial row and equates the remaining polar node values. This enforces one common scalar origin value.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialScal.text: Requires a first-order jet class in both variables. Near-origin and far-field orders may be supplied jointly by the explicit radial factor and vanishing endpoint jets.

Breakdown.PotentialShape.IsPotentialSeri.text: The G and U amplitudes have C¹ joining and the required decay; flux joining is required in its normal direction; pressure has separate axis and origin constraints. These are sufficient formal conditions for the analytic properties of (B.51), not a recovered file format.

Breakdown.CellCert.Finite.quadValue.text: Evaluates the real matrix form on a real vector. Symmetry and positivity are separate requirements, so this evaluator alone supplies neither.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.curlComp.text: The component formula reads the gradient entry with output index first and derivative index second. That convention must be kept when comparing the paper's printed curl array.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBase.text: Stores coefficient functions for every natural degree in r and z. A finite file therefore needs a specified continuation beyond the degrees it stores.
Evaluates degree j using only coefficients numbered zero through j. Coefficients outside that range do not affect this polynomial.
Evaluates degree l using the height coefficient table. Orthonormality is imposed by IsCellBases, not by the evaluator.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.IsCellBa.text: The radial basis is orthonormal with lineWeight and the height basis with ordinary measure, with positive leading coefficients at every degree. These requirements fix normalisation and signs beyond the truncated cell unknowns.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.radialEi.text: Uses j(j+2) on axis cells and j(j+1) off the axis, with the square of the inverse half-width. Degree zero has eigenvalue zero.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.heightEi.text: Uses the Legendre eigenvalue l(l+1) with the square of the inverse half-height. The degree-zero value is deliberately zero.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.sumSq.text: Adds squared complex moduli of all nine gradient entries, with no symmetry reduction.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.vecSq.text: Adds squared complex moduli of the three velocity components.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.curlSq.text: Forms curlComp first, then sums the three squared moduli; it is not a sum over all nine entries.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.pairVec.text: Packs nine gradient entries in row-major order 3a+b, then the three velocity entries. This fixes the coordinates of the 12 by 12 matrices in (B.26).

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellScal.text: Collects polynomial cutoffs, resolved modes, local matrix fields and tail-absorption weights for the reusable one-frequency estimate. The active certificate supplies corresponding data separately for each space-time label.
Divides cylindrical measure r by the basis weight. On an axis cell this agrees with one away from the axis; at r=0 Lean's total division gives zero.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.ParamData.text: Stores selected relation rows, the unknown solved by each row, and retained skeleton unknowns. It does not itself assert that the solved block is invertible.
Extracts the square submatrix by looking up the selected solved coordinate in each relation row. Its determinant is tested by IsParamData.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsParamDa.text: Requires distinct solved coordinates, no solved coordinate in the skeleton, and a nonzero determinant for the solved block. It does not say that all remaining coordinates are skeleton coordinates.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.quadFormV.text: Uses the conjugate of the first vector in the complex matrix pairing and returns its real part. Hermitian symmetry is a separate condition.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.edgeSign.text: Chooses the sign from the relative order of the face and opposite-face coordinates. Equality is excluded separately by the face-validity predicate.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.radialStr.text: Expresses a trace moment by an integral over the strip between a face and its opposite. The denominator is the signed face separation, and the final test polynomial depends on height.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.heightStr.text: The corresponding strip integral differentiates in height and retains a supplied radial weight. Face orientation and the radial measure are independent choices.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.FaceSegme.text: Stores face direction, face and opposite-face coordinates, interval endpoints and polynomial test coefficients. The opposite face is needed for the strip representation of a trace.
Evaluates the finite coefficient prefix for the requested degree. The family remains indexed by every natural degree even when the certificate uses only finitely many.
Selects a radial or height strip according to the segment direction. The weighted flag changes the radial measure only for height strips.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsFaceSeg.text: Requires a nonzero strip width, positive interval length and nonzero leading test coefficient at every degree. Finite polynomial tables need a continuation satisfying the last condition.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.presMode.text: This helper takes a normalised angular Fourier coefficient at fixed r and z. It has a single angular integer and no time transform; active space-time modes are supplied later.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayou.text: Lists volume coefficients, side and pressure segments, corners and auxiliary side coefficients. Optional corner references represent the special axis case, not arbitrary missing data.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellDatum.text: The disjoint sum distinguishes gradient, velocity, side, pressure, corner, stream and extra-side data. The corner-stream block has no harmonic label, unlike the seven other blocks.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayou.text: Specialises the eight tagged blocks to the layout's harmonic set, degrees, segment counts and corners.
Provides classical equality for the finite tagged coordinate type. This instance is a logical convenience and is not a serialised comparison routine.
Derives finiteness from the tagged product-and-sum construction. A decoder's packed ordering must agree with the chosen coordinate map.
Radial faces use height polynomials; height faces use radial polynomials with an extra factor r on axis cells.
The tagged index separates derivative identities, divergence, axis conditions, stream identities and side-moment consistency. Different tags have different degree ranges.
Integrates a supplied one-variable test against a segment polynomial over that segment's interval.
This helper uses ordinary one-dimensional measure; callers insert lineWeight explicitly when it is needed.
Integrates over the closed height interval. Boundary endpoints have no extra mass in the integral.
Pairs a derivative of one radial basis polynomial with another, using lineWeight and the reference-interval vanishing factor.
Pairs a height derivative with a basis polynomial using the corresponding reference-interval factor.
Represents multiplication by r in the weighted radial basis through an integral of two basis polynomials.
