Returns the row that reads one tagged datum. It is an exact algebraic coordinate selector.
Returns the coordinate row when both degrees lie through Q, and the zero row otherwise. The fallback is intentional and must not mask a malformed stored index.
Returns a velocity-coordinate row only for degrees below Q, with zero outside that range.
Combines multiplication by the angular frequency with rotation of the cylindrical basis. The radial and angular components acquire opposite frame-coupling terms.
Returns an extra-side coordinate row through degree Q and zero beyond it.
A present corner selects its stream coordinate; an absent corner contributes zero. Layout validity restricts the absence to the permitted axis case.
Looks up zero in the layout's finite mode set. The optional result controls axis and stream relations that exist only for that mode.
Axis cells use powers r^(i+2), while off-axis cells use r^i. The shifted exponent supports the axis boundary identities.

Builds the ten families of exact linear relations from differentiation, divergence, axis behaviour and trace matching. Some index cases deliberately produce zero rows; independent selected rows are checked later.
Marks side velocity, side gradient, pressure, corner velocity and corner stream blocks as skeleton data. Volume and extra-side coefficients are excluded.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsCellLay.text: Matches the abstract cell data, degrees and bases, then imposes exact side placement, coverage and orthonormal trace tests. Axis omissions and polynomial degree restrictions are explicit parts of the predicate.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.IsCellPar.text: Identifies every elimination row with a row of relationRow and restricts the retained skeleton to skeleton data. It deliberately keeps the selector and solved-block data explicit.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.CellLayou.text: Reads a corner component when the cell-corner map is present and otherwise gives zero. The layout predicate controls which axis corners can be omitted.
Combines segmented gradient moments with the integrals of a whole-side test against each segment test polynomial.
Uses r₁ for side zero and r₂ otherwise. Its geometric interpretation requires the caller to be in a radial-side branch.
Maps whole-side number two to the lower height endpoint and the other branch to the upper one.
Maps side zero to the inner radial endpoint and the other branch to the outer endpoint.
Combines velocity moments on the side's segments, retaining the q+2 test range.
Applies the angular-frequency and cylindrical-frame terms to the assembled side velocity row.
Reconstructs a face gradient from tangential integration by parts, angular frame terms or stored normal derivative moments, according to the component and face.
Replaces the normal diagonal entry by minus the other two diagonal entries. This implements the divergence-free trace constraint on either kind of face.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellFormula.radialWei.text: Integrates ρ times the supplied test function from zero to r. This is a helper for weighted trace identities, rather than a new certificate condition.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.formOfRows.text: The returned matrix is the conjugate-row pullback of the supplied form. Complex conjugation is on the first row factor.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.testSupFor.text: Pulls back the inverse test Gram matrix. The inverse is total in Lean; the analytical use needs the separate positive-definiteness hypotheses.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.LowIndex.text: Abstracts the map from a cell's gradient and velocity coefficients and face rows to a larger coordinate set.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.basisFn.text: Multiplies one radial and one height basis polynomial, with normalisation supplied by the basis predicate.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.monomial.text: Uses ordinary r and z powers, unlike CellPoly.eval, which uses affine reference coordinates.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialSlop.text: Differentiates a real test function while fixing height; regularity is a separate mathematical input.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightSlop.text: Differentiates a real test function while fixing radius.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.rectIntegr.text: Uses ordinary two-dimensional measure. Callers supply the cylindrical or polynomial-basis radial weight explicitly.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.testInnerM.text: Forms a complex matrix from real weighted integrals of pairs of tests. It does not itself assert positivity of the weight or matrix.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.frameTurn.text: Records the two nonzero coefficients that couple radial and angular basis directions under rotation.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularCom.text: Combines the harmonic frequency with frame rotation in both indices of a gradient array.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularArr.text: Applies angularComb to a linear combination of gradient components, retaining both frame corrections.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.unitArray.text: The coefficient array isolates a single ordered gradient entry, without imposing symmetry.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.curlArray.text: The alternating array extracts the appropriate difference of gradient entries with the same convention as curlComp.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.lowRow.text: Combines low-gradient coordinate selectors with the supplied component array at one harmonic and one polynomial index.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialFace.text: Combines stored radial-face rows with an array selecting gradient or curl components.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightFace.text: The height-face version keeps the same component convention and its own polynomial-index direction.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.lowPairRow.text: Expands a test pairing through the known low-gradient coefficients, using integrals against tensor-product basis functions.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightMome.text: Integrates a power of z against a height basis polynomial over the cell interval.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialMome.text: Integrates a power of r against a radial basis polynomial with the axis-dependent lineWeight.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialProj.text: Forms the derivative contribution already determined by low coefficients, including innerRadius and the reference vanishing factor.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightProj.text: Forms the corresponding height derivative contribution using the height reference coordinate.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialInne.text: The weight combines r−r₁ with the radial reference vanishing factor and is used by the off-axis inner form.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightInne.text: Combines r−r₁ with the height reference vanishing factor for the off-axis inner form.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialInne.text: Uses an inverse Gram matrix on degrees below Q−1 in radius and through Q in height. Natural subtraction makes the index empty for small Q.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightInne.text: Uses the integration-by-parts test family with degrees below Q in both variables and the height inner weight.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.radialOute.text: Multiplies a meridian monomial by the basis lineWeight; this is a test function, not a coordinate value.
Combines moments on both radial faces with a differentiated interior test. The displayed plus signs follow the reference-coordinate factors already included in the formula.
Pairs the radial outer rows through the inverse Gram matrix with cylindrical weight r.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.heightOute.text: Combines height-face moments and an interior derivative of r times the height reference coordinate and test monomial.
Uses the inverse Gram matrix for height outer rows, with the radial and height degree ranges in their stated order.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularTes.text: Adds a factor r to the monomial so that the angular test family has the required axis behaviour.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularAxi.text: Uses the axis-compatible tests and a Gram matrix with radial weight r, avoiding a separate inverse-radius diagonal term.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.angularOff.text: The weight is (r₂−r)/(r r₂); the off-axis branch and valid cell provide the positivity and denominator conditions.
Adds an inverse-r₂ diagonal form to a weighted test-supremum remainder. It is selected only in the off-axis component form.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.componentF.text: Combines radial, height and angular contributions, choosing different constructions on and off the axis.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.topForm.text: Selects the upper degree strips of two gradient-column blocks. Its use of Q−1 is natural-number subtraction.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.energyForm.text: Sums component derivative forms with mode weights and subtracts the prescribed highest-degree penalty.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.LowSlot.text: The two constructors distinguish a nine-component gradient basis element from a three-component velocity element, with different degree cutoffs.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotValue.text: A gradient slot has zero velocity and a velocity slot has zero gradient. Each nonzero component is one tensor-product basis function.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotIndex.text: Routes a gradient or velocity slot through the corresponding map in LowIndex.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.slotRow.text: The row is one at the embedded slot and zero elsewhere; it includes a harmonic label as well as the slot constructor.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.matrixSesq.text: Evaluates the full complex sesquilinear expression on two packed 12-component vectors, before a real part is taken elsewhere.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellEnergy.layoutInde.text: Connects abstract LowIndex to the tagged CellDatum slots and translates two radial plus two height faces into the four-side numbering.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.polyFn.text: Describes functions representable by complex coefficients with separate radial and height degree cutoffs. It is a set of functions, not a stored coefficient array.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.CellBox..text: Integrates F times the complex conjugate of the test polynomial with a supplied real weight.
Integrates the squared complex modulus against a supplied weight. Nonnegativity requires the weight assumptions used by the estimate.
Lifts the one-dimensional basis weight to the meridian rectangle without introducing a height dependence.
Chooses a polynomial orthogonal residual when such a polynomial exists, and returns zero otherwise. The analytic projection properties require the separate existence and uniqueness arguments.
Measures the residual after projection through degree Q in both variables, with the polynomial-basis radial weight.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.sesqValu.text: Evaluates the real part of the complex form on the packed gradient-velocity vector, using conjugation on its first factor.

Breakdown.CellCert.CellAnalysis.supremum.text: Implements the three terms of L(G,v): curl, mixed gradient-velocity, and a Young-inequality split with length ℓ. Positivity of ℓ is a separate requirement.

Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.quadForm.text: Takes the real part of the conjugate matrix pairing. It uses the same convention as the local Hermitian forms.

Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.inverseWeigh.text: Evaluates the form of D inverse on a complex vector. Positive definiteness of D makes this a squared norm; the total matrix inverse alone supplies no positivity.

Breakdown.CertCell.Coupling.realQuadForm.text: Casts every real matrix entry to complex numbers before taking the real quadratic form. This is not an entrywise absolute-value bound.

Breakdown.CertCell.ModeCoefficients.ofPi.text: Reads the class and harmonic-dependent weights into the five scalar coefficients. The subtraction of c in I₂ and the share term in I₂′ remain explicit.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.tailGain.text: The gain combines the first omitted radial/height eigenvalue with the positive-part angular gain. Axis cells use innerRadius=1 in the radial factor.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.hessTailGain.text: The angular shift is 2 for a gradient tensor, giving the (|κι₁|−2)₊ term in (B.27).

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.curlTailGain.text: The angular shift is 1 for a vector such as curl v, giving the corresponding omitted-mode gain.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.velTailGain.text: The velocity coefficients use degree Q−1, so the first omitted spectral level is Q instead of Q+1.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.text: The record separates Hessian and curl-gradient floors from lower-order absorption, potential and leakage charges, which are combined in Holds.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.v.text: The total velocity absorption, potential and leakage cost is replaced by its positive part before division by the velocity spectral gain.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.g.text: Any curl absorption not covered by the curl-gradient spectral gain is charged twice to the gradient, using |curl u|²≤2|∇u|².

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.TailBudget.H.text: The remaining gradient, potential, leakage and converted velocity charges must fit beneath the Hessian floor times its spectral gain.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.text: The five squared-derivative coefficients and one cross coefficient represent the f₂, f′₂, f′₁, f₁, f₀ and f₀₁ quantities used before (B.29).

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.cu.text: The curl-gradient coefficient contributes its (k−1)₊²/r² gain to the curl coefficient.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.gr.text: The Hessian angular gain and the negative part of the curl coefficient are combined into f₁*; only a negative curl coefficient needs the factor 2.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.ve.text: The allocated nonnegative gradient share t adds t(k−1)₊²/r² to f₀.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.Pa.text: All four inequalities in (B.29) are required, including the discriminant inequality for the cross term.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.EntryCharges.text: The three bounds s₁,s₂,s₃ and the positive scale h feed the stretching loss; a′₁,a₁,a₀ and c_* describe the additional unresolved-mode charges.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.wi.text: The modified coefficients subtract s₁+a′₁, c_*s₃h/2+a₁ and c_*s₃/(2h)+a₀, and add c_*s₂ to the cross term.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.PointCoef.ch.text: The point-dependent charge functions are evaluated first and then passed to the explicit coefficient update.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.EntryCharges.text: Every mode in the supplied set and every point of the region must share the stated upper bounds and the same strictly positive length h.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.CreditPatch.text: The rectangle Π carries real test functions and a positive test-form candidate, together with a real trace map and a complex credit matrix on selected trace coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.CreditPatch.te.text: Coefficients are conjugated before multiplying the real test functions; this fixes the sesquilinear convention of the subsequent form comparison.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.CreditPatch.tr.text: The real trace matrix is applied to the complex moment vector to produce the test-coordinate vector.

Breakdown.CertCell.Bridge.IsCreditPatch.text: The trace expansion, weighted Dirichlet upper bound and inverse-form comparison must use the same test functions and matrices. Bounds for charge and test regularity have domains larger than the rectangle itself.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsHarmon.text: The generic fractional-cell layout predicate is specialised through auxiliary data with no actuator or global-row coordinates; only its order and resolved angular modes are prescribed here.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellMode.text: Every label selects a layout and a parameterization of its relation space, while all labels share one orthonormal cell basis.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellMo.text: Each resolved label has skeleton degree at least one and its layout degrees match the mesh. The selected relations must provide the stated cell parameterization.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.coefPair.text: The curl, gradient and velocity terms act on a complex 3×3 gradient and a complex three-vector, before Hessian terms are added.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.LeafValu.text: The leaf stores the two high-derivative floors, a Hermitian 12×12 local form candidate and separate absorption and polynomial-model error penalties.
The penalty combines curl, gradient and velocity squares with the three box-error coefficients.
The second penalty has the same three quadratic channels but different coefficients, reserved for the stretching/pairing estimates.
The three stored absorption coefficients charge curl, gradient and velocity squares when controlling the omitted polynomial tail.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafVa.text: The local matrix must be Hermitian and bounded measurable, and its comparisons hold for every complex gradient/vector pair. Hessian positivity is strict, while curl-Hessian positivity is non-strict.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsSplitP.text: The high and long pieces are bounded separately; the remaining error is full minus model minus both pieces, uniformly in time and space on the selected solid.
Only the residual inequality is almost everywhere in the meridian plane; outside one null set it holds for every time and angle. The high and long bounds remain pointwise.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsVecOrt.text: Every label and component has zero moments against all rectangular monomials with each degree at most the supplied bound; the integral here has no additional radial weight.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsMatOrt.text: Every label and matrix component has the corresponding zero polynomial moments, again with ordinary meridian-plane measure.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.vorticit.text: The vorticity is curl W formed from the spatial Fréchet derivative at each normalized time.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.strainOf.text: The strain is the symmetric part (∇W+(∇W)ᵀ)/2 of the real linear derivative map.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.vorticit.text: The contraction of the prescribed Hessian supplies ∇curl W, allowing the weak reference Hessian convention to be used.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellMode.text: The four high pieces represent velocity, vorticity, strain and vorticity gradient and are later required to have vanishing low polynomial moments.
The four long pieces carry an angular cutoff and their own error bounds; their low angular modes are excluded by IsCellModelSplit.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCellMo.text: Each of the four fields is split into model, high, long and residual parts. Orthogonality, angular gaps, symmetry, measurability and nonnegative error budgets are separate obligations.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.testValu.text: The three CellPoly components are evaluated using the cell's coordinate convention before row integrals are formed.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.turnVect.text: The operator ikx plus the frame-rotation correction mixes the radial and angular components, while the vertical component has only ikx₃.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.testGrad.text: Radial and vertical columns use spatial derivatives; the angular column is turnVector divided by r. Axis regularity is checked separately.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsTestSo.text: The cylindrical divergence equation is multiplied by r, giving ∂r(rϕr)+ikϕφ+r∂zϕz=0 throughout the cell rectangle.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsAxisRe.text: The angular numerator is bounded by a constant times r on the entire cell, controlling the division by r in the angular derivative.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sideTest.text: The face-moment routine receives the scalar test and both meridian derivatives, with its non-pressure convention selected explicitly.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.basisVal.text: A radial and a vertical real orthonormal polynomial are multiplied and embedded in ℂ for use in complex row integrals.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.frameWei.text: The cylindrical components of y are r,0,z; this helper inserts the corresponding component in the similarity-drift row.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownStrai.text: The integral includes radial measure r, the conjugated test gradient and half the coordinate times the conjugated test value.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownVeloc.text: The velocity pairing is multiplied by i times the supplied physical frequency plus 1/2, with radial integration weight and conjugated test value.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sideGrad.text: The boundary coefficient has a negative outward-orientation factor; a radial side also contributes its constant radial coordinate.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.sidePres.text: The pressure trace pairs with the normal test component and the positive outward-orientation factor, using component r or z according to the side.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.ownRowVe.text: Only the low-gradient, low-velocity, gradient-side and pressure-side blocks receive coefficients; every other tagged coordinate block is zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsTestOf.text: The degree limits are (q,q−1), (q,q) and (q−1,q) for the r,φ,z components, with Lean's natural-number subtraction at q=0.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.coupling.text: Two alternating-symbol contractions encode the cross-product coupling, integrated against the basis, radial weight and conjugated test field.
The vorticity model enters the alternating-symbol contraction paired with a low-velocity coefficient and a conjugated test component.
The coupling acts only on the low-gradient and low-velocity blocks, with all boundary and auxiliary blocks zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.opBound.text: The squared bound holds for every complex three-vector. Since c appears squared, nonnegativity of c must come from the surrounding charge conditions when needed.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsCharge.text: The strain form, mean vorticity-gradient operator and its oscillating remainder provide s₁,s₂,s₃ on every resolved label and point of the cell.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.BoxConst.text: The record stores the source and length weights, strain slack, per-label row weights and an orthogonal-tail weight used in the error accounting.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.IsLeafBo.text: The polynomial-model errors and reciprocal-period error are charged to the corresponding box and pairing penalties, with positivity conditions on the auxiliary weights.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.lowSlotF.text: The local matrix is integrated against tensor-basis slot pairs and pulled back by the slot rows; different angular slots have zero cross coefficient here.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.lowStrai.text: Each gradient component uses tensor polynomial coefficients through degree Q in both variables, indexed by the mode's tagged lowStrain coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.lowVeloc.text: Each velocity component uses tensor coefficients below Q in both variables, giving degree at most Q−1 rather than the gradient's degree Q.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.CellCalc.text: The conditions combine layouts and uniform leaf bounds with model decomposition and trace placement. Pressure segmentation is required before the extra prohibition of radial pressure traces on the axis.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.modeBloc.text: The block adds the Hessian/curl-Hessian energy form to the integrated lower-order 12×12 form; the third energy-form coefficient is set to zero here.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellCalculus.energyLe.text: The resolved-mode energy blocks are assembled diagonally and embedded into the full cell index; ports and the two actuator/pin blocks receive zero energy entries here.

Breakdown.CertCell.CreditEval.IsPlaneSid.text: The selected coordinate must be a side-velocity moment of the vertical component on the lower plane, with matching segment endpoints and test function.

Breakdown.CertCell.CreditEval.CreditEval.text: Every credit coordinate matches the patch's physical harmonic and the correct plane-side moment, and the whole rectangle lies in the mesh.

Breakdown.CertCell.InstancePair.IsPairSu.text: Pin profiles are exact on every label, and forcing-gradient profiles are exact off the declared slack set. The weighted L² error on that set is summed over every forcing field and bounded by the cell error budget.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.SignedTre.text: Stores finite leaf, node and column types, their placements, local fronts and pivot slacks. It does not itself prove that parent pointers form an acyclic rooted tree.
Sums the leaf forms attached to the node and the fronts of all nodes whose parent is this node. The parent relation is read literally, including any cycle a later predicate allows.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesPiv.text: Requires every global unknown to be pivoted with positive slack, a nonnegative root front, and no more global columns than free unknowns. Both sets of global unknowns are included in pivot coverage.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.pivotDiag.text: Places the supplied slack only on pivot coordinates, with zeros elsewhere.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.slackRema.text: Subtracts pivot slack, positive column squares and the outgoing base, while adding the negative-column square. The signs are those inside the weighted row bound (B.40).

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.complexDi.text: Casts the real pivot diagonal to complex coefficients without changing its support.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.complexSl.text: Uses conjugate transposes in both column products. Replacing these by ordinary transposes would certify a different form.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.ofRealVec.text: Casts the global real vector into complex coordinates before applying a complex node's coordinate matrix.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.realRestr.text: Pulls a complex matrix back along E and takes the real part of every entry. The resulting real form acts on global real unknowns.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.realColum.text: Transforms each complex column and produces separate real and imaginary columns, each scaled by the square root of t. Zero or repeated numerical columns still occupy distinct indexed slots.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.Coordinat.text: Each complex coordinate may read one real slot and one signed imaginary slot, with either absent. This representation does not assert a globally injective coordinate map.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.IsCoordin.text: For pivot coordinates, the imaginary sign has square one and the real and imaginary slots cannot be the same. No analogous restriction is imposed here on nonpivot coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.Coordinat.text: Builds each row from its optional real slot and signed imaginary slot. Missing slots contribute zero rather than causing a decoding failure.
A real unknown is owned if it appears in either the real or imaginary slot of the complex coordinate.
Collects all real slots owned by the complex pivot set. Multiple pivot coordinates may contribute to the same real slot.
Sums the slacks from all pivot coordinates using a given real unknown. It does not select a single representative owner.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.SignedTre.text: Places a global column in this node's matrix exactly when its recorded node matches; all other entries are zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.RealNodeD.text: Stores the approximate input and base matrices, pivot values, positive scaling weights, error radii and positive factor columns. Symmetry and inequalities belong to PassesRealNodeEnclosure.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.ComplexNo.text: Adds a coordinate representation and nonnegative factor to Hermitian node data, with separate positive and negative column families. The negative columns must later be injected into twice as many real column slots.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesRea.text: Combines quadratic input/front bounds with nonnegative symmetric error matrices, positive row weights and the weighted residual bound. These are universally quantified inequalities, not merely small matrix residuals.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesCom.text: Certifies the node in complex coordinates, translates pivot slacks and injects the real and imaginary parts of each negative complex column into global columns. The nonnegative factor may be zero only when the other pivot and slack conditions still hold.

Breakdown.CertCell.Certificate.PassesNod.text: A node may satisfy either enclosure branch, with branch-specific data and error matrices. A checker must preserve the existential witness and the disjunction.

Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.GaugeKeyValu.text: Stores the pressure gauge classes, deleted coordinates and an exact rational inverse for their incidence matrix. These are extra data behind the paper’s unspecified global coordinate relations.
An endpoint contributes one precisely when its optional class equals the requested gauge class; an absent endpoint contributes zero.
Only zero-azimuthal pressure keys with the matching harmonic class contribute. Radial faces use a one-dimensional moment, while horizontal faces use a weighted endpoint difference.
Embeds the real pressure gauge moment into ℂ without adding an imaginary component.
Returns a pressure-key moment and zero for other key kinds. The horizontal value uses the upper radial primitive; it is not the endpoint difference used by a full gauge direction.
Evaluates the key weight at the pressure coordinate chosen for deletion; the gauge conditions later require this number to be nonzero.
Rows index deleted pressure coordinates and columns index gauge classes. This fixes the orientation of the incidence comparison.
Scales each row of the integer incidence matrix by that deleted coordinate’s real integration weight, then views the result as complex.

Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.keyMode.text: Extracts the mode of velocity, gradient, pressure and corner keys; stream keys carry mode zero and private coordinates have no skeleton mode.

Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.planeSign.text: Attaches a parity only to keys on z=0. Velocity and gradient moments have opposite frame signs, pressure is even, and the stream value is odd.

Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.RealLabelOmi.text: Marks only an imaginary coordinate at harmonic zero with skeleton mode zero as absent by reality.

Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.PlanePairOmi.text: For the specified positive diagonal family of labels, reflection and reality remove one real or imaginary component according to the key’s parity.

Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.PlaneOddOmit.text: Marks mode-zero plane keys with odd reflection parity as absent.

Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.GaugeKeyValu.text: A key is deleted only when it occurs in the stored list with exactly the same harmonic label.
The rational inverse, conjugation rules and nonzero integration weights make the deletion scheme meaningful. A numerically approximate inverse does not satisfy these identities.

Breakdown.CertCell.globalForm.text: The global upper bound is the negative β-square with coercivity and global error, plus the negative ζ-square. Substituting 3/50 and 1000 recovers the constants of (B.43).

Breakdown.CertCell.realLeafForm.text: Computes the real matrix of the pulled-back complex form using the conjugate transpose of P. Its argument coordinates are real global unknowns.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.text: Supplies the two finite sets of global real unknowns, local embeddings, leaves and node data used by (B.38)–(B.40). Geometry and algebraic validity are imposed separately, so constructing this record is not checking the tree.

Breakdown.CertCell.keySeg.text: Builds the segment used to interpret a common boundary key. Its unused opposite level is chosen as lev+1, so this helper must not be confused with a cell’s physical width.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.Leaf.text: Leaves distinguish A₀, ordered cell blocks, signed null-pair occurrences and rectangle credits. The nested sum preserves these cases even when some index sets are empty.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.leafFintype.text: Combines the recorded finite enumerations to enumerate all four leaf kinds. It adds no numerical positivity condition.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.pieceForm.text: Masks the cell matrix to a chosen row-part and column-part. An off-diagonal block need not be Hermitian by itself; its transposed partner is placed at the same node.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.creditEmbed.text: Selects from each owning cell’s embedding the coordinates used by a rectangle credit. Different entries may come from different cells.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.leafForm.text: Converts cell blocks to real global forms, inserts each null pair with both signs, and doubles the rectangle-credit form. These factors are the assembly identity in (B.38).

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.leafNode.text: Uses the relevant node field for each leaf kind, including a separate node for each sign of a null pair.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.tree.text: Combines the tree data with candidate front matrices Vξ. The front matrices are witnesses supplied to the node and pivot-count conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.gaugeDir.text: Places pressure gauge moments in the cell’s skeleton coordinates and zero in ports and both multiplier blocks.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeConditionsGiven.text: Requires a unique root and one common family of front matrices that passes every node enclosure and the global pivot count. The existential witness is shared across all nodes.

Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.unitMoment.text: Computes the full face moment of a unit pressure value. Horizontal faces use a difference of weighted primitives, distinguishing this from a deleted-key endpoint weight.

Breakdown.CertCell.GaugeKey.KeyInHalfPla.text: Requires positive radius for radial faces and corners, allows zero radius for horizontal segments and stream values, and imposes no geometry on private coordinates.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.KeyPartOmit.text: A real or imaginary component may be absent through reality, plane parity or an explicit gauge deletion. The plane cases additionally require the key to lie in the permitted half-plane.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.varDir.text: Uses a cell-coordinate gauge value first; multiplier unknowns contribute zero; otherwise a common skeleton key supplies the gauge value. Missing keys contribute zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.varPartDir.text: Combines a gauge class with its conjugate class to obtain the real or imaginary coordinate direction. This is a pair of class directions, not ordinary numeric extraction from one entry.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.GaugeRowTra.text: For every non-deleted cell key, its direct gauge direction equals the row representation acting on global gauge directions.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.GaugeKeyCon.text: Requires pressure gauges to lie in both left and right kernels of cell forms, to vanish on credit coordinates, and to reconstruct unit pressure moments.

Breakdown.CertCell.TreeEntry.RealKeyCond.text: Checks that standalone skeleton unknowns carry the mode recorded by their label, and that every cell key lies in the permitted half-plane.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyWithMode.text: Replaces the mode in velocity, gradient, pressure and corner keys while preserving geometry; stream and private keys remain unchanged.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyOnPlane.text: Recognizes horizontal face keys at z=0 and corner or stream points on that plane. A private coordinate is never classified as a plane key.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyFlipSign.text: Returns the frame parity for velocity and corner data, the opposite parity for gradient data, one for pressure, and the axial parity for the stream value.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.sideKeyGeom.text: Extracts side orientation, level, interval, polynomial tests and degree from velocity, gradient or pressure keys. Other key types return none.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.retileKey.text: Changes a face key’s interval, polynomial test family and degree while keeping its field type, mode and orientation. Non-face keys are left as they were.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.presUnitMome.text: Evaluates the face moment contributed by constant pressure, including the mode convention of the layout. Every non-pressure coordinate receives zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.headUnit.text: Extends the constant-pressure moment to a single resolved harmonic of the full cell-coordinate vector, with zeros in the other harmonics, ports and multiplier blocks.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.keyVelNormal.text: Recognizes a mode-zero velocity moment in the component normal to its radial or horizontal face. These are the keys that can be reconstructed from stream endpoint values.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ConjDatum.text: Matches each of the eight datum kinds with the opposite azimuthal mode and the same relevant geometry. Matching indices alone is insufficient when two layouts differ.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.streamEnds.text: Returns the lower or upper geometric endpoint, with the variable coordinate chosen according to the face orientation.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.KeyEvaluatio.text: Stores a target harmonic, whether to conjugate, and a real parity factor. IsKeyEvaluation constrains these values to one of four valid symmetry cases.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsKeyEvaluat.text: Allows direct reading, complex conjugation, reflection on z=0, or their combination. The reflected cases require both plane geometry and the prescribed key parity.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsKeyVar.text: Identifies a purely skeletal global unknown: both the cell and multiplier evaluations must be absent, while key, harmonic and real/imaginary choice must agree.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PartBound.text: A stored component must be a matching global skeleton variable. An absent component needs a proved omission reason or an axis stream value at r=0.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.partVec.text: Builds a complex linear functional from optional real and imaginary global slots, changing the imaginary sign under conjugation. If both options name the same slot, both contributions are added.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.SplitChoice.text: Stores a subdivision, local test bases and coefficient expansions of a parent face moment, together with optional global coordinates and stream endpoints. SplitRow supplies all geometric and algebraic checks.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FluxChoice.text: Stores the symmetry reading and the optional real and imaginary stream values at the two ends of a face. FluxRow supplies the moment identity and denominator checks.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowReason.text: A row is justified by a shared key, a subdivision, a flux identity, a derived relation, a normal-derivative relation, a directly evaluated leaf, or an unused-coordinate proof.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowReason.Is.text: This predicate is true only for the unused constructor. It does not check the matrix-zero facts that make an unused row valid.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.text: Stores each row as a finite support and complex coefficients, with an explicit justification and a rank for recursive dependencies. Ports use natural keys, so their coordinate maps have an infinite declared domain.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.row.text: Extends the stored row coefficients by zero outside rowVars. Coefficients outside the support are ignored rather than implicitly included.
Sums the supported complex coefficients against real global unknowns. Realness of the input is part of the coordinate model.
Builds X_Q from row vectors, optional complex ports and the β,ζ selections. The two port slots may share indices, so their contributions must be added exactly.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Key.text: Excludes private keys, checks the symmetry evaluation and both optional components, then requires exact equality with the resulting complex row vector.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.til.text: Constructs the segment for one tile of a face-moment subdivision using its local interval and test coefficients.

Uses stream endpoint differences to reconstruct the constant normal-velocity moment. The radial branch divides by the face radius; the horizontal branch divides by the leading linear test coefficient.
Uses the stream-flux formula only for a tile marked flux and degree zero. All other local moments use their optional direct real and imaginary slots.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Spl.text: Requires a nonempty contiguous tiling, exact test-polynomial identities, valid shared coordinates and justified flux substitutions. The resulting row equality is exact, with every listed coefficient included.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Flu.text: Provides separate radial and horizontal moment identities. The horizontal branch also requires the linear velocity moment to have smaller rank and to be used.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.rel.text: Forms the coefficient of one datum in a finite linear combination of the layout’s relation rows.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Der.text: The chosen combination has coefficient one on the target and zero on pressure data. Every other nonzero coefficient uses a non-unused row of smaller rank, giving a well-founded reconstruction.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Lea.text: Binds the real component to a cell datum and allows an optional imaginary component. Omitting the imaginary component is permitted only at harmonic zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Unu.text: Requires the sparse row itself, the entire row and column of the cell matrix, and every credit use to vanish. The coordinate remains free in InRowRange.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.vel.text: Reads the requested side-velocity row when its natural degree fits the layout and returns zero beyond that range.
Requires a valid in-range degree, a strictly smaller rank than the target, and a justification other than unused.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.cor.text: An absent corner returns the zero row. A present corner uses the corresponding cell velocity datum.
Requires all three corner-velocity components to have smaller rank and a non-unused justification.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Nor.text: Uses the face divergence relation, polynomial test derivatives and endpoint velocities to determine a normal gradient moment. An absent lower corner is permitted only on a horizontal segment starting at the axis.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowEntry.Acc.text: Dispatches on the seven row-reason constructors and asks for that constructor’s exact justification. This is the complete row-level obligation, rather than a tag-only test.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TreeRowCondi.text: Links the stored X_Q to the row construction, supplies the A₀ upper bound (B.43), and makes pressure heads invisible. The field named global_eq is a one-sided inequality.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellVars.text: Includes the resolved cell data, auxiliary ports, β coordinates and ζ coordinates. The type is larger than the polynomial velocity coefficients alone.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsRegionChar.text: The paper’s s₁,s₂,s₃,h are represented as curl, product, gradient and length charges. The length is required to be positive and independent of the harmonic label on the region.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CellBlocks.text: Stores the matrices P_Q,B_Q,T_Q, eliminated-mode data and row-functionals used in (B.26). The record also carries error costs needed to absorb unresolved couplings; none of those inequalities is proved merely by supplying the record.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.AssemblyEntr.text: Associates each cell with blocks indexed by that cell’s complete coordinate type, including ports and both multiplier blocks.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.restrictData.text: Reads only the resolved-coordinate summand for one harmonic. Ports and the β,ζ blocks are excluded by the sum-type injections.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.linearField.text: Forms a finite complex linear combination of the stored coefficient fields using the supplied cell vector. No conjugation is applied to the input coefficients.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.creditVelDem.text: Adds the rectangle charge exactly where the harmonic is the reflected rectangle label or its negative and the point lies in the rectangle. This is part of the unresolved velocity budget.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.turnMatrix.text: Encodes the angular derivative in the rotating cylindrical frame at integer azimuthal mode n. Its singular modes are n=0 and n=±1, excluded for eliminated modes by band_turn.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.totalStrainC.text: Adds the potential, pairing and row contributions charged against the resolved gradient tail.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.totalVelCost.text: Adds the potential and row contributions charged against the resolved velocity tail; there is no separate pairing velocity charge.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EntryCharges.text: The bounds are uniform in the harmonic label on each cell. The common bound also controls the charge length above and through an inverse lower bound, so simple point sampling is insufficient.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FieldRegular.text: Collects the weak second-derivative model, its harmonic expansion, admissibility and measurable coefficient bounds. It supplies analytic prerequisites that a finite matrix check alone cannot establish.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.AssemblyRegu.text: Adds bounded measurability of pairing surrogates and every local matrix entry to the field and charge hypotheses. Bounds may depend on the listed indices, according to their quantifier order.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.sourceSum.text: Adds the potential source and finite-dimensional pairing source before the angular square completion.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.gradSlot.text: Embeds the nine gradient indices as slots 0 through 8 of the twelve-component gradient/value vector.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.turnedVec.text: Corrects precisely the angular-derivative gradient column using the adjoint entries of the inverse angular matrix and the last three velocity slots.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.turnedSource.text: Applies the cylindrical angular correction at the harmonic’s actual azimuthal frequency to the combined potential and pairing source.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.turnedRowBan.text: Applies the same angular correction to one row’s eliminated-mode coefficient field.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandEliminat.text: Defines b_Q as a radial-weighted integral of a quadratic square-completion expression over eliminated modes. The division by bandSlack is paired with an exact vanishing condition when that slack is zero.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.rowsEliminat.text: Defines e_Q from the row vector after subtracting its eliminated-mode coupling, using the inverse-weighted square for rowFull.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandGram.text: Integrates the conjugate product of turned row fields with radial weight and inverse gradient weights. The order of the two row indices fixes the Hermitian convention.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsBoundedOnC.text: Requires both almost-everywhere strong measurability and a pointwise finite bound on the entire closed cell rectangle.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.EliminationC.text: Imposes the local matrix comparison (B.26) on the domain S, together with positivity and regularity needed for its eliminated-mode formulas. In the final condition S is InRowRange.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.TailConditio.text: Matches each harmonic’s tail budget to the local Hessian floors and allocates all potential, pairing and row costs. The top matrix is assembled by an exact weighted sum.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.topValue.text: Weights selected edge bands of polynomial gradient coefficients by inverse radial and vertical eigenvalues. The radial and vertical summands use different degree tests and gradient directions.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.testAt.text: Evaluates the stored test-field polynomial on the physical cell rectangle.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.rowGram.text: Rows from different harmonic labels have zero pairing. Equal-label entries integrate one test times the conjugate of the other with radial weight r.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.scaledRowGra.text: Divides a same-harmonic Gram block by the scalar attached to its row’s harmonic label. Positivity of that scalar is established by the surrounding row conditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.leakGram.text: Uses the leakage weight as the harmonic block scale of the row Gram matrix.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.rowBaseWeigh.text: Uses the certificate’s test weight to scale each harmonic block of the row Gram matrix.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.tailGramPart.text: Integrates either the nine gradient slots or the three velocity slots of the tail tests using the cell’s line weight, which differs from r on non-axis cells.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowCondition.text: The indexed rows must enumerate every declared tested pair exactly once, with positive Gram and leakage weights. Their matrix domination must include both resolved tail remainders and unresolved leakage.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.lowGrad.text: Sums the low polynomial gradient data over the internal cell modes of one resolved harmonic.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.lowVel.text: Sums the low polynomial velocity data over the internal cell modes of one resolved harmonic.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.lowProfile.text: Packs the nine gradient entries followed by the three velocity entries into the vector on which the local 12×12 matrices act.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.sesq12.text: Uses conjugation on the first vector and no real-part extraction. Later integration or quadratic-form definitions choose when to take the real part.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelBilin.text: Expands the three model stretching and transport contributions using the strain, vorticity gradient and alternating symbol. It is bilinear in the two gradient/value pairs before conjugation is supplied elsewhere.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelTriple.text: Averages the bilinear model expression with the expression in the swapped pair of arguments. This symmetrisation is distinct from taking a Hermitian adjoint.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.velOf.text: Reads slots 9,10,11 from a twelve-component gradient/value vector.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.gradOf.text: Reads gradient entry (a,b) from slot 3a+b, fixing the tensor order used in every twelve-component matrix.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.pairArray.text: Reindexes a curried 3×3 array as a function on pairs. It changes indexing only and applies no transpose or symmetry operation.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.splitCharge.text: Adds separate squared-norm costs for the curl, full gradient and velocity of one mode.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialDat.text: Encodes the model convolution, the matrix used to split kept data, harmonic groups and Young-inequality costs. The paper describes the role of P_Q but does not specify this full record.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingData.text: Stores the harmonic set, positive weights and Gram forms that control tails of the β and 2ζ pairing profiles.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.CouplingEntr.text: Keeps the potential data and finite-dimensional pairing data together for each cell, with its own coordinate type.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.isPressureDa.text: Recognizes the pressure summand in the nested CellDatum representation. The decision depends on the sum-type constructor, not a numerical coordinate range.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.upperPart.text: Returns x−Px for the supplied bandProjection matrix P. This decomposition is meaningful without assuming that P is an orthogonal projection.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.bandPart.text: Returns Px for the supplied bandProjection matrix. Together with upperPart it sums exactly to x.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.epsOwnCharge.text: Applies the curl, gradient and velocity split to local reference-model errors, with the two separate positive lengths used in the formal estimates.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longFactor.text: Uses longBalance up to the absolute azimuthal-label cutoff and 1+1/longBalance above it. Equality with the cutoff belongs to the low branch.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longOwnCharg.text: Multiplies the distant strain and vorticity-gradient split by the low/high long-range factor.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.groupCharge.text: Balances a group’s vorticity-gradient bound between full-gradient and velocity costs, with its chosen matrix constant and positive length.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.couplingPair.text: Integrates all resolved harmonic pairs with coupling label ι−ι′ and the radial weight r. The order of that difference is part of the convolution convention.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.absorbValue.text: Evaluates the curl, gradient and velocity absorption reserved in the leaf data for one resolved harmonic.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.potentialExa.text: Combines upper-upper and twice upper-selected couplings, then subtracts selected local forms, port costs and group, local-error and distant-harmonic charges. PotentialConditions bounds the stored P_Q by this expression.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.strainOfVec.text: Despite the name, this helper only reshapes the first nine entries into a 3×3 array. It does not replace the gradient by its symmetric part.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.lowAt.text: Returns the low profile at resolved labels and the zero twelve-vector at all other labels. This is an explicit zero continuation, not an inferred sparse default.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.upperProfile.text: Applies the resolved-profile zero extension to the complementary cell vector x−Px.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.highOwnCharg.text: Forms the high-error curl, full-gradient and velocity penalty from the three Young weights.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.highOwnAmoun.text: Sums that penalty over an explicitly supplied finite harmonic set and integrates with cylindrical weight r on the cell.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.couplingTail.text: Computes a polynomial-orthogonal tail using degree d for gradient slots and d−1 for velocity slots. The source includes both convolution against other resolved profiles and the same-harmonic local matrix.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.rHatMax.text: Uses the outer radius divided by the line weight there. It equals one on an axis cell and the outer radius on a non-axis cell once the cell is valid.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelLabels.text: Filters the four declared support sets by exact nonvanishing of a velocity, vorticity, strain or vorticity-gradient coefficient somewhere in the cell. Three separate coverage conditions use this set.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PotentialCon.text: These fifty-seven fields make the kept potential comparison, harmonic coverage, error absorption and analytic hypotheses explicit. The comparison is required on S, instantiated as InRowRange in CellLayerEntryConditions.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.pairWeightOf.text: The forcing block is read unchanged and the pin block is multiplied by two, matching the coefficients of the B_Q pairing.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.pairingProfi.text: Forms the complex linear combination of stored pairing profiles with the β,2ζ weight vector.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.pairingExact.text: Pairs resolved polynomial gradients with the weighted forcing/pin profile, then subtracts the Gram penalty for all selected gamma harmonics. The integral carries the cylindrical factor r.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.PairingCondi.text: Bounds B_Q on S and controls the nonzero pairing tails in both resolved and unresolved modes. The Gram inequalities quantify real β,ζ weights even though the matrices are complex.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.rowTestPoly.text: Selects the three polynomial components using the row’s harmonic label and natural test index.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelVelocit.text: Reads the three velocity components at one model harmonic and point.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.modelVortici.text: Reads the three vorticity components at one model harmonic and point.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.crossTest.text: Encodes the velocity/vorticity cross-product terms as a twelve-component test. Its nested conjugations fix how this complex test pairs with a perturbation.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.rowCrossTest.text: Uses the difference between the row’s harmonic and the source harmonic to select the model coefficients in the cross test.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.actuatorRow.text: Integrates one forcing harmonic against the conjugated polynomial test with radial weight r.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.deactSources.text: Takes all tested-label minus reference-label differences, then removes resolved and eliminated modes. These finite differences must be included in the leakage set.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.activeGroups.text: Selects coupling groups whose row-partner set can produce the row label through a group harmonic difference.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longRowCost.text: Chooses the low or high row cost according to the validated low-label predicate.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longSourceCo.text: For a low source label uses the high cost, and for a high source label uses both low and high costs. This differs from longRowCost.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.longRowTerm.text: Returns zero only when both long-range velocity and vorticity errors vanish exactly; otherwise it returns the reciprocal row cost.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.RowFunctiona.text: Identifies rowMap, band tests and orthogonal remainders with the actual equation, then allocates all error costs. The record mixes exact identities, finite harmonic coverage and estimates uniform in the parameter set.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.InRowRange.text: Only used cell coordinates must agree with one real row vector plus arbitrary complex gauge and pressure-head contributions. Unused cell coordinates and ports remain arbitrary complex values, while both β and ζ blocks must be real.

Breakdown.CertCell.PotentialEntryConditi.text: This is an implication: once eight analytic and geometric prerequisites are supplied, the potential conditions must follow. Those prerequisites are obtained elsewhere in the complete cell route.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerEntries.text: Combines local matrices, coupling data, unresolved-mode and exterior covers, exterior value sets and the global-row representation. These witnesses are shared by the conditions that follow.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellLayerEntryConditi.text: These twenty fields connect the local forms, tested rows, exterior estimates and global tree. The three local form inequalities all use the same InRowRange domain, while separate blindness conditions justify pressure and gauge transport.

Breakdown.CellCert.Exterior.traceFreeCon.text: This is the square root of seven halves appearing in the mixed gradient-velocity loss. It is the fixed constant before any larger exterior majorant is chosen.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.SetPieceBoun.text: One record can cover an infinite harmonic set when its class, signed piece membership, frequency bounds and coupling envelopes are uniform there.

The coefficient includes the negative Hessian norm of Zι, λ losses and the μ-frequency gain with its transport and coupling penalties.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsOffModeCon.text: The region is a measurable subset of the open quarter-plane, and the charged scalar form must pass (B.29) at every point there.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeRadius.text: The radius √(r²+z²) is the full spatial distance |y| in cylindrical coordinates, not the cylindrical radius r.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeRayRegi.text: The exterior is the part of the open quarter-plane lying strictly beyond the direction-dependent radius.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.planeSquareE.text: A point belongs when either r or z exceeds the supplied edge, still restricted to r>0 and z>0.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsDirectionR.text: The radius function is measurable, uniformly bounded above and below by a positive number, and homogeneous of degree zero under positive dilations.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.rayInverseSq.text: The admissible radial-exterior constant is 1/4+(k−1)₊², combining radial Hardy and angular derivative gains.

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.ExteriorCond.text: The record carries Λ₀ and the three bounds f₁∞, f₀∞ and f₀₁∞ needed to control an unbounded region by (B.30).

Breakdown.CertCell.TailBand.IsExteriorCo.text: The shape is either a bounded positive radial graph or a square exterior with zero azimuthal modes. The pointwise coefficient envelopes and final scalar test use the same Λ₀.

Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientEntry.text: Stores bounds on unresolved regions and fixed lower coefficients on resolved or eliminated modes. The regions and mode sets can be infinite, so a finite list of entries still describes continuum obligations.

Breakdown.CertCell.CoefficientConditions.text: The complement condition quantifies every label and every point with r>0 and z≥0, including points outside all cells. The velocity coefficient floor is weighted by r²+z².

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.OffModeCover.text: Stores finitely many regional conditions and, for each cell and every integer harmonic, a finite selection of them. The selector’s infinite domain needs a mathematical decoding rule.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsOffModeCov.text: Covers the positive-radius part of every cell for every non-resolved harmonic, including eliminated harmonics. Each selected region must contain that harmonic and dominate the required entry charges.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.ExteriorCove.text: Combines ray-type exterior entries with ordinary pointwise regions. Every harmonic chooses parts from this common finite collection and all parts use one charge family.
Selects the region from the ray-condition or point-condition branch of the tagged exterior index.
Selects the possibly infinite harmonic set from the appropriate tagged exterior entry.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.IsExteriorCo.text: Requires the selected regions to cover precisely the exterior up to null overlaps and supplies measurable, bounded charges. Validity applies to every stored entry, even one not selected for a particular harmonic.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldValu.text: Supplies chart-based upper bounds for the strain, mean vorticity gradient and oscillatory vorticity gradient used outside all cells.

Breakdown.CertCell.Assembly.FarFieldCond.text: Binds the three chart enclosures to the exact exterior model charges and gives a positive harmonic-independent length h. The field bounds hold at every time and angle on the full exterior.

Breakdown.CertCell.CellHypothesis.text: Collects seventeen requirements behind the first field of CellSystemCondition, including shape data, tree checks, analytic bounds and the constants 39/50, 3/50 and 1000. It remains a hypothesis about decoded data.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CertificateCla.text: Collects the sign, residual, contraction, parameter-inclusion and nontriviality inequalities left unchanged from Section 7. Positive weight and positive period are supplied elsewhere in CellSystemCondition, so this record must not be checked in isolation.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CoerciveNumber.text: Names the uniform multiplier-weight bounds n_λ, n_{∇λ}, n_μ of (B.19), together with the total cell error n_b. The same globalError is supplied to the cell and entry conditions.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbers.text: Separates the error from the fixed reference to the centre profile and the additional error over the parameter set. Their gradient bounds use different Lebesgue exponents.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ShiftNumbersBo.text: The derivative operator norm is measured in spatial L² for the centre error and spatial L³ for the parameter-dependent error, at every time. Their two weighted sums feed the linearization gap and frozen-form shift.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.PotentialEntri.text: Stores one harmonic potential series and chart per multiplier coordinate, together with shared pin representations. Only selected adjoint coordinates need their series validated.
Requires valid shape data and exact equalities to the potentials and pins used by the adjoint-defect entry. The shared pinField equality ties all multiplier coordinates, not only those in J.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.ReductionEntri.text: Collects the witness data that turn the cell estimates into the Section 7 certificate. Shared profile, pressure, adjoint and potential entries must retain the same identities throughout the reduction.

Breakdown.CellLayerSystem.CellSystemCond.text: This conjunction is the precise conditional premise of the exported cell theorems. It requires one shared set of seven data arguments and does not construct or verify a concrete numerical certificate.
